煞地神相貌丑陋、身材短小、生性贪婪，他扬长避短，练得一手掘地穴行的独门功夫，因此被度天王收服做了一头领，常年拦路抢劫。
煞地神贪婪奢靡，不满足于抢劫的微薄收入。他听过不少神话传说，尤为喜爱各类恶神，认为那些恶神肆意妄为，为害一方，反倒让民众害怕，主动奉上香火，甚是痛快。因此他也认为自己那话本里说的“奇人异相”，乃星宿下凡。他本身就有遁地的功夫，因此扮成土地神，占一处土地庙，强迫附近居民日夜供奉，还美其名曰“消灾解难”。若有不找他消灾的，煞地神也不啰嗦，马上让灾难兑现。因此有不少不懂规矩的过路客商遭殃。
煞地神仍觉得日常供奉还不足供他享用，因此最爱办道场。一场热闹的盛会既能让他享受到大量的金银酒肉，也能欣赏到乡民对他的“敬怕”。现下煞地神又在他盘踞的土地庙前，摆起了本月第二场道场，静候乡民路人前来供奉。
en:
The Earth Fiend Deity is ugly, short, and greedy by nature. Playing to his strengths and avoiding his weaknesses, he mastered a unique tunneling martial art, burrowing and moving through the ground. Because of this, he was taken in by Chieftain Du and made a subordinate leader, spending his days waylaying travelers and robbing them.
But the Earth Fiend Deity's greed knew no bounds, mere roadside robberies could not satisfy him. Having heard countless myths and legends, he grew especially fond of tales about evil deities, believing that those who brought terror to the land were rewarded with offerings of incense and devotion born of fear. Thus, he came to see himself as a "wondrous being descended from the stars," just like the strange heroes and freaks of old storybooks. Thanks to his burrowing abilities, he disguised himself as a local Earth God, took over a village shrine, and forced the nearby villagers to offer sacrifices day and night, all under the pretense of "warding off disasters." Any who refused to pay tribute quickly found calamity striking at their doors, and many were unsuspecting merchants who met misfortune on the road.
Still unsatisfied with daily offerings, the Earth Fiend Deity turned to hosting grand rituals. Such lively gatherings not only showered him with gold, silver, food, and wine, but also fed his pride as he watched the fearful reverence of the people. Today, he has already prepared the second ritual of the month outside the shrine he occupies, eagerly awaiting fresh offerings from passing villagers and travelers alike.

Now, when the master returns from work, he's drenched in sweat and panting, barely able to say a few words before falling into a deep sleep. By the time Buddy wakes up, he's already out the door again.
This won't do. So Buddy decided to get up early in secret, push several wooden buckets over, and surround his master to block his way.

zh:
一个陈旧的猫窝，还沾着几根白色的猫毛。 

你少时常见到寒姨抱着一只白猫，这便是它的猫窝。奇怪的是，这猫窝做工粗糙，像什么人手编而成，不如寒姨惯用之物那般精致。
身为小少东家的你也试过拿了几个又漂亮又新的猫窝给小白，但它总会睡回那个旧窝。
直到后来小白大了，小窝睡不下了，才被寒姨换了去。
当时你问寒姨，那个旧猫窝去哪了，寒姨只说丢了。如今，它又被你的猫翻捡了出来。
原来，它从没被丢掉，也没被烧毁在那场大火里。
en:
An old cat bed, with a few strands of white fur still clinging to it.

When you were little, you often saw Aunt Han holding a white cat. This was its bed. Strangely, it's roughly made, as if someone wove it by hand, nothing like Aunt Han's usual refined belongings.
As the young master, you once brought Snowball several newer, prettier beds, but it always went back to this old one. Only after it grew too large to curl up inside did Aunt Han replace it.
You asked what happened to the old bed, and Aunt Han only said she'd thrown it away. Yet here it is again, dug out by your cat.
It was never discarded, nor was it lost in that fire.

It counts as one.
I count as one too.
It went in.
I went in too.

An endless spring flows here, its waters chiming with a clear, crisp melody.
The town is named after it, and the people thrive on its purity. In the local schools, young children study etiquette and music from dawn till dusk. Here, warriors wash their hands in golden basins, cleansing away the bitter grudges of the Jianghu. Escort flags flutter under the sun, protecting merchants on their long journeys. The aroma of cooking smoke rises alongside the scent of books, and the endless spring flows alongside the spirit of chivalry. Travelers need not search for the mythical Peach Blossom Spring, for the scenery and heart of this town hold all the warmth one could desire.

Lu Yao, a man of Hedong. His family had tilled the soil for generations. In the second year of Kaiping, he joined the army on campaign.
Over thirty-eight years of service, he rose step by step to the post of Supervisor. Though he never broke an enemy line nor slew an enemy general, in all the grain and fodder that passed through his hands, there was never once an error.
He marched with the army on many campaigns. At Yunzhou, at the siege of Taiyuan, and at the battle of Yangcheng, he was there among the ranks, and never once turned back in the face of danger.
In the third year of Kaiyun, stirred by the call of the wandering heroes, he escorted provisions to Zhongdu Bridge.
No place will be given him in the histories, nor any line in the rolls of merit. It is enough that Heaven and Earth, and the millet itself, should know.

襄阳府密报节略

近月以来，城仓廒新筑十座，皆贮米麦，车运自汴、洛来者，昼夜不绝。继粮草后，诸路兵卒渐次屯集，营帐连郭，炊烟竟日不散。

军旅既众，市井顿繁。浆洗、刍秣、负贩、庖厨诸役，需人甚急。茶贩、酒贩、饼贩络绎于道，蜀、楚商贾亦负货而至
……
管粮官于城外设场收籴，价从优给，乡民争粜，肩担车推，道为之塞。又有贩马者自西行，马二百匹，皆良驹，径入襄阳军营，营中夜闻蹄声，至晓乃止。

右件皆弟子亲勘，谨录以闻。续有风动，嗣当驰报。
en:
Xiangyang Prefecture Secret Report Summary

Over recent months, ten new granaries have been built in the city to store rice and wheat. Carts transporting supplies from Kaifeng and Luoyang arrive day and night without rest. Following the provisions, soldiers from various routes are gradually gathering. Their tents stretch all the way to the city walls, and the smoke from their cooking fires lingers all day long.

With all these troops around, the markets are bustling with activity. There is an urgent need for labor in washing, fodder handling, portering, and cooking. Tea, wine, and pastry vendors crowd the streets. Merchants from Shu and Chu are showing up with their goods.
...
The grain official set up a purchasing station outside the city at favorable prices. The locals are practically fighting each other to sell, carrying sacks and pushing carts until the roads are completely blocked. On top of that, horse traders from the west brought two hundred fine horses directly into the Xiangyang military camp. Hooves stomped all night long, and it didn't stop until dawn.

Your disciple has personally verified these truths and recorded them for your eyes. Any further developments will be reported immediately.
AndromedaWrath
Zhuo Chen
Li Xinyu

zh: 君子六艺，礼、乐、射、御、书、数。  鸦虽为墨门中人，却总会鼓励弟子不拘于墨学、博采众派所长。 昔年燕、隼、鹭三人曾共用一把旧弓习射。 至最后一堂射术，恰课结弓断。鸦笑说几人已入新境，当与旧别，再启新程。  后燕、隼、鹭三人出师后，竟不约而同带了新材来修这把旧弓。   “弓之道，需和其肢体，调其气息，一其心志，缓引之，急射之……”  预为良弓需得良材，欲为良工需有良才。不知这六材弓，下一次开弓急射是何时。
en:
The Six Arts of the gentleman: rites, music, archery, charioteering, calligraphy, and mathematics.

Though Raven was a Mohist, he always urged his disciples to look beyond Mohist teachings and learn from every school.

Years ago, Swallow, Falcon, and Heron practiced archery with the same old bow. On their final lesson, the bow snapped right as class ended. Raven only laughed, saying they'd reached a new stage, and that it was time to part with the old and set out anew.

After the three completed their training, they each brought fresh materials to repair that old bow.

"The Way of the Bow lies in setting the limbs in harmony, steadying the breath, and fixing the will. Draw slow, and release swift..."

A fine bow needs fine materials; a fine craft needs fine talent. One can only wonder when this Six-Material Bow will be drawn and loosed again.

怎么他们不去那繁华的市楼，甘愿来这灯火阑珊处？漩儿一直想不明白。难不成，这水里有什么好玩的东西？
平生从未沾过水的漩儿，小心翼翼地将爪子垂入水面。一瞬间，它看到自己的倒影碎成银鳞，和月的波光交融在一起。
好玩！好玩！
从此世界上多了一只爱玩水的小猫。
en:
Many come to the water's edge alone, lost in thought for hours on end. Whirl quietly follows, hearing soft sobs or seeing some gaze wordlessly at the moon's shimmering reflection. 
Why don't they go to the bustling market? Why seek this quiet, fading glow? Whirl could never understand—was there some magic in the water? 
Having never touched a drop before, Whirl gently dipped a paw into the surface. In that moment, its reflection shattered into silver scales, merging with the moonlight's dance. 
How mesmerizing! How enchanting! 
From that day forward, a little cat who loved the water was born.

#Y【是英雄眠处。】你曾亲身走进狮子下的英雄冢，见证了他们为天下太平做出的努力。万千人之心，万千人之愿，乃太平归处。#E
听闻你所言，几位弟子面面相觑。他们挠挠头，半晌才开口说道，此处过去不过是一片荒野，如今赫然出现石狮子，或许是地气地脉异动；另一位则坚持认为此地有帝陵，那狮子便是引路标……见无人与你接话，你也只得暗自苦笑。你回头看了看那只最大石狮子，它依然安静地昂首迎风而立，岿然不动，千古如一。
en:
Outside the little hut at Homeward Wilds, several Inkbound Order disciples are in the middle of a lively debate over the origins of the stone lions. One is certain they once stood along the spirit way of an imperial tomb; another insists they are merely an artisan's flourish, nothing more than a display of skill; a third is convinced that some long-lost treasure must lie hidden beneath them. The moment they spot you, they crowd around at once, chattering over one another to offer their theories and ask what you think...
#Y[This is where heroic souls rest.] You once walked into the Tomb of Heroes beneath the lions and saw for yourself all they gave for peace under heaven. It bears witness to the hearts and wishes of the thousands of people. There lies the home of peace.#E
At your answer, the disciples fall briefly silent and trade bewildered glances. They scratch their heads, and after a long pause, someone ventures that this place used to be nothing but wilderness, so perhaps the sudden appearance of the stone lions is due to some strange stirring in the earth's veins; another still refuses to yield, insisting there must be an imperial tomb here, with the lions marking the way... With no one quite able to follow your meaning, you can only let out a wry, inward smile. Turning back, you look once more at the largest stone lion. It still stands there quietly as ever, head lifted proudly into the wind, immovable, timeless, unchanged through the ages.
Where'd you come from, little one? Hungry?

历城人认识成怀瑾的，都知道她打小是个闲不住的。别家孩子还在赖床，她已经沿着山路跑了个来回。
跑还不老实跑，非要高抬腿，膝盖顶到胸口。街坊嬉笑问她，怀瑾啊，你这是练的什么功？她认真道，练腿功。腿练好了，才能跑得快，跑得快了，才能多做事。
多做事，是她顶要紧的事。文津馆的书生们跑来跑去的做事，青州也跑，天下也跑，成怀瑾便拜入了文津馆。
可是，文津馆只是个起点。她在馆里可以读书做事，背着老奶奶爬山、下海捞鞋、帮人跑腿，那从文津馆离开呢？江湖需要她吗？朝堂需要她吗？青州的乡亲们都说文津馆的小夫子无所不知，可在这里就有个满是问题的小弟子。
她做的这些事，能算作履历吗？
能的吧。
她做得这些事，能真正的帮上人吗？
能的吧。
可万一不能呢？万一她跑遍了天下，也没有一个地方要她呢？万一她满腔热血，最后只能冷在某个角落里呢？
每当成怀瑾脑袋里冒出这些问题，便加倍地跑、加倍地帮。剿匪、探路、扛米、救人，不放过任何机会。多干一些，多实践一些，多得一些经验，那些问题，好像便追不上她了。
en:
Ask anyone in Licheng, and they'll tell you Cheng Huaijin has never been able to sit still. Even as a kid, while everyone else was still fast asleep, she'd already be running laps up and down the mountain paths.
She didn't just jog, either. She bounded, driving her knees high to her chest with every stride. When amused neighbors asked what kind of bizarre martial arts she was practicing, she'd answer completely deadpan: "Leg work. Strong legs mean I run faster. If I run faster, I can get more done."
To Huaijin, "getting things done" was all that mattered. She watched the scholars of the Inkbound Order constantly on the move, putting in the work across Qingzhou and the world beyond. Naturally, she decided to join their ranks.
But the Inkbound Order was only ever meant to be a stepping stone. Sure, she could read and run odd jobs there: carrying elders up steep trails, diving into the ocean to fish out dropped shoes, running errands for the locals, but what would happen when she finally left? Would the jianghu actually need her? Would the imperial court? Folks in Qingzhou always said the young scholars of the Inkbound Order knew everything, yet here she was, a little disciple burdened by endless questions.
Did all these random chores actually count for anything?
She liked to think so.
Was she actually making a difference?
She liked to think so.
But what if she wasn't? What if she traveled to the ends of the earth and couldn't find a single place that wanted her? What if all her burning passion eventually just flickered out in some cold, forgotten corner of the world?
Whenever those creeping anxieties started to flare up, Huaijin's answer was simply to run twice as fast and work twice as hard. Hunting down bandits, scouting dangerous roads, hauling heavy sacks of grain, and saving lives, she threw herself at every single opportunity. She figured if she just kept working, kept pushing, and kept herself moving, the doubt would never be fast enough to catch her.
Huh? What now?

她什么都好，就是爱做梦。每天清早把万一揣在怀里带到历城台，往操场边一放，先出一套软绵绵的拳，然后蹲下来摸着猫头让万一好好学，说等你当了顶梁柱，咱家就靠你了！

大伙儿笑得前仰后合。万一不动声色，每天蹲在场上跟人练拳，伸爪划拉划拉。
唉，有这样一个不靠谱的主人，猫猫也只能努努力，用小肩膀扛起重担了呦！
en:
Chancey's owner is named Liu Niannian. She is wonderful in every way, except she loves to daydream. Every early morning, she tucks Chancey into her arms and brings it to Licheng Terrace. Setting it down by the training field, she first performs a set of soft, languid punches. Then, she squats down, strokes the cat's head, and tells it to watch carefully. "Once you become the breadwinner, our family will be counting on you!"

Chancey simply licks its paws, too lazy to make a sound.

Liu Niannian never gives up. She even signs the cat up for training classes, telling everyone she meets, "Do not underestimate it just because it is a cat now. What if it gains spiritual awareness? What if it becomes a magical spirit? What if... it can actually turn around and provide for me!"

The crowd always bursts into laughter. Chancey remains completely unfazed. Every day, it squats on the field, practicing alongside the others by lazily taking a few swipes in the air.

Alas, with such an unreliable owner, the little kitty has no choice but to work hard and carry the heavy burden on its tiny shoulders!

不甘，是成年后的石贞，最多的情绪。
沙场出身，耻辱尚未洗刷，燕云未复，却良弓早藏，他不甘。
义父作为一方大将，殚心竭虑，一心为国，却甘心放权。他不甘。
延庆公主，与他素有情谊，却因联姻安抚，许配给了他年幼的义弟石保吉。他不甘。
不甘，但又能如何呢？没有办法。
他带着这情绪沉入地下。一感到不甘时，便会去地底操练，一遍遍地练，生怕自己忘了那份手感，忘了那份初心。这套动作他练了无数次。
但有一天，闯入了一个人，容鸢。
这阵子，容鸢总是有意无意的主动接近，石贞能感受到她对他立场的试探。对于这种替官家卖命的人，他一向敬而远之。容鸢也察觉到了，但在给武庙制作机关时，还是会偶尔过来，默默坐着，一人沉思，一人练枪，互不打扰。

”你，不甘么？“容鸢突然问道。
”……，嗯。“
”我也是。“

这是他们之间，除了公务之外，唯一的对话。
石贞奇怪，她有什么不甘的，给朝廷造船，威风凛凛的容将军。于是他开始在意起来。也开始从各处，从义父那里开始逐渐了解她的过去，她的如今。
他好像逐渐理解了容鸢。思考着，他拿着随便摘来的小草，随便的扎了只蜻蜓。这是他小时在边陲与老士兵学的。这蜻蜓……倒是与那鸢挺像的……
好吧，下次，等她再来时。自己便与她好好聊聊吧。
但不久之后，便得到了她炸船身陨的消息。

这套动作他练了无数次，体会了如此多的不甘，不会再有什么事情能打乱他的思绪。
“是吧？”他的动作停下了，复而一笑，继续操练。
“将军，发生什么事了么？”士兵小心翼翼地问道。
“没有。”
”可是将军，你的动作好像做错了……“
en:
Resentment clung to Shi Zhen like a second skin in adulthood.
He resented the battlefield that forged him, yet left him unvindicated. His honor was still stained, the territories still unreclaimed, his blade sheathed too soon.
He resented his adoptive father, a revered general who'd surrendered power willingly despite his lifelong loyalty to the crown.
He resented Princess Yanqing, whose childhood bond with him meant nothing when politics wedded her to his callow younger brother, Shi Baoji.
Resentment festered, useless and inescapable.
He buried that bitterness underground, drilling combat forms until muscle memory eclipsed thought. Never forget, he'd tell himself with every strike. Never soften.
Then Murong Yuan crashed into his solitude.
Lately, Murong Yuan had been circling him, subtle probes about his loyalties. As someone who served the imperial court, she should've repelled him. Yet during her work on the Martial Temple's contraptions, she'd linger silently in his training yard. They coexisted like parallel stars: her sketching blueprints, his sparring shadows, neither acknowledging the other.

"Does it eat at you too?" she asked abruptly one day.
"...Yes."
"Same."

That single exchange, stripped of formalities, haunted him.
What could she resent? The famed "Admiral Rong," architect of the empire's warships, seemed untouchable. Curiosity gnawed at him. He began piecing together her past and present from others and his adoptive father.
He started understanding Murong Yuan. While idly twisting grass into a dragonfly (a childhood skill learned from frontier soldiers), it struck him: the dragonfly was practically Murong Yuan remade...Next time she comes, he decided, I'll talk to her.
But "next time" never came. News of her death arrived weeks later. In a shipyard explosion, no body recovered.
Shi Zhen resumed his drills, movements sharper than ever. Nothing left to unsettle me now, he thought.
"Well?" He stopped, and with a smile, he continued practicing.
"General, what happened?" A soldier cautiously asked.
"Nothing."
"But General, you got the wrong move..."

zh:
【文公第六】

元年春，王正月，公即位。
〇二月，癸亥朔，日有食之。
〇天王使叔服来会葬。其言来会葬何？会葬，礼也。
〇夏四月，丁巳，葬我君僖公。
〇天王使毛伯来锡公命。
锡者何？赐也。命者何？加我服也。
〇晋侯伐卫。
〇叔孙得臣如京师。
〇卫人伐晋。
〇秋，公孙敖会晋侯于戚。
〇冬十月，丁未，楚世子商臣弑其君髡。
〇公孙敖如齐。

二年春，王二月，甲子，晋侯及秦师战于彭衙，秦师败绩。
〇丁丑，作僖公主。
作僖公主者何？为僖公作主也。主者曷用？虞主用桑，练主用栗。用栗者，藏主也。作僖公主何以书？讥。何讥尔？不时也。其不时奈何？欲久丧而后不能也。
〇三月，乙巳，及晋处父盟。
此晋阳处父也，何以不氏？讳与大夫盟也。
〇夏，六月，公孙敖会宋公、陈侯、郑伯、晋士縠，盟于垂敛。
〇自十有二月不雨，至于秋七月。
何以书？记异也。大旱以灾书，此亦旱也，曷为以异书？大旱之日短而云灾，故以灾书；此不雨之日长而无灾，故以异书也。
〇八月，丁卯，大事于大庙，跻僖公。
大事者何？大祫也。大祫者何？合祭也。其合祭奈何？毁庙之主，陈于大祖，未毁庙之主，皆升，合食于大祖，五年而再殷祭。跻者何？升也。何言乎升僖公？讥。何讥尔？逆祀也。其逆祀奈何？先祢而后祖也。
〇冬，晋人、宋人、陈人、郑人伐秦。
〇公子遂如齐纳币。
纳币不书，此何以书？讥。何讥尔？讥丧娶也。娶在三年之外，则何讥乎丧娶？三年之内不图婚。吉禘于庄公，讥。然则曷为不于祭焉讥？三年之恩疾矣，非虚加之也，以人心为皆有之。以人心为皆有之，则曷为独于娶焉讥？娶者，大吉也，非常吉也。其为吉者主于已，以为有人心焉者，则宜于此焉变矣。

……
en:
【Duke Wen, Part Six】

First year, spring, the king's first month, the duke assumed the throne.
〇Second month, on the day Guihai, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
〇The Son of Heaven sent Shufu to come and attend the funeral. Why does it say "come to attend the funeral"? Attending a funeral is a matter of propriety.
〇Summer, fourth month, on the day Dingsi, we buried our ruler Duke Xi.
〇The Son of Heaven sent Maobo to come and bestow upon the duke his mandate.
What does "bestow" mean? It means to grant. What does "mandate" mean? It means to confer upon us robes of office.
〇The Marquis of Jin attacked Wei.
〇Shusun Dechen went to the capital.
〇The people of Wei attacked Jin.
〇Autumn, Gongsun Ao met with the Marquis of Jin at Qi.
〇Winter, tenth month, on the day Dingwei, Shang Chen, the heir apparent of Chu, assassinated his ruler, Kun.
〇Gongsun Ao went to Qi.

Second year, spring, the king's second month, on the day Jiazi, the Marquis of Jin fought a battle with the Qin army at Pengya, and the Qin army was defeated.
〇On the day Dingchou, the spirit tablet for Duke Xi was made.
What does "making the spirit tablet for Duke Xi" mean? It means making a spirit tablet for Duke Xi. What material is used for the spirit tablet? For the mourning tablet, mulberry wood is used; for the tablet after the mourning period, chestnut wood is used. Using chestnut wood means the tablet is to be stored away. Why is making the spirit tablet for Duke Xi recorded? To criticize. What is criticized? That it was not done at the proper time. What was improper about the timing? He wanted to prolong the mourning period but later could not do so.
〇Third month, on the day Yisi, he made a covenant with Jin Chufu.
This is Jinyang Chufu; why is his clan name not given? To avoid recording a covenant with a high official.
〇Summer, sixth month, Gongsun Ao met with the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, and Jin Shihu, and they made a covenant at Chuilian.
〇From the twelfth month there was no rain, up to the seventh month of autumn.
Why is this recorded? To note an anomaly. A great drought is recorded as a calamity; this was also a drought, so why is it recorded as an anomaly? In a great drought, the period is short and it is called a calamity, so it is recorded as a calamity; in this case, the period without rain was long and there was no calamity, so it is recorded as an anomaly.
〇Eighth month, on the day Dingmao, a great ceremony was held at the Grand Temple, elevating Duke Xi.
What does "great ceremony" mean? It is the great combined sacrifice. What is the great combined sacrifice? It is a joint offering. How is the joint offering conducted? The spirit tablets of destroyed temples are placed before the Grand Ancestor, and the spirit tablets of temples not yet destroyed are all raised up to share in the offering before the Grand Ancestor, with a grand sacrifice every five years. What does "elevating" mean? It means raising up. Why does it say "elevating Duke Xi"? To criticize. What is criticized? The violation of sacrificial order. What was the violation? Placing the father before the grandfather.
〇Winter, the people of Jin, Song, Chen, and Zheng attacked Qin.
〇Gongsun Zi went to Qi to present betrothal gifts.
Presenting betrothal gifts is not usually recorded; why is this recorded? To criticize. What is criticized? Criticizing marriage during mourning. If the marriage takes place after the three-year mourning period, then why criticize marriage during mourning? Within the three-year period, one should not plan a marriage. The auspicious sacrifice to Duke Zhuang was criticized. Then why not criticize at the sacrifice? The grace of the three-year mourning period is profound; it is not added in vain, for it is believed that all people possess such feelings. If it is believed that all people possess such feelings, then why criticize only in the matter of marriage? Marriage is a great auspicious event, not an ordinary auspicious one. The auspiciousness is centered on oneself, and for one who is thought to possess such feelings, one should change in this matter.

zh:
田英曾是文津馆的弟子，因为天资卓越而崭露头角。
听闻，他翻遍了文津馆所有的藏书。又听闻，每本藏书，他都只翻三页。
田三页的名号，逐渐传到了馆内泰斗长乐老的耳中。
或许是可惜英才，或许是不满行事，长乐老将田英召来询问。
田英却如此对答：“英无意学识，唯寻心中之路而已。”
他想从那些书中，寻找什么样的路，却无人知道。或许连他自己也不知道，他只是一遍遍埋首在浩如烟海的书籍中，寻找答案。

后来，田英终于寻到了想要追寻的那条路，却不是从书中，而是从那个魏先生身上。
魏先生说，《春秋》之上，没有仁义忠勇。
那是以身为火炬的人，见过的人不会再忘，只会随即点燃自己的火焰。
田英就这么跟随着魏先生，离开了文津馆。

他已知道自己的路。
en:
Long before this night, Tian Ying was a disciple at the Inkbound Order, famed for his brilliance.
 It was said he read every book in the Hall, yet in each, he read only three pages.
Hence, the nickname 'Tian of Three Pages' began to spread, eventually reaching Elder Chang Le, the venerable master of the Hall. 
Whether out of admiration or disapproval, he ultimately summoned Tian Ying and asked why he read in such a mean way.
Tian Ying replied, simply, "I do not seek knowledge. I seek the path in my heart."
What path he searched for in those books, no one knew. Perhaps not even Tian Ying himself. He simply kept reading, page by page, diving into the vast sea of ink.

Eventually, Tian Ying found what he was looking for; not in books, but in a man called Master Wei.
He once said, "Kindness, righteousness, loyalty, and courage are nothing more than words found in the Spring and Autumn Annals."
He burns like a torch, and anyone who encounters him will never forget, instead igniting their own flame.
And so, Tian Ying follows him, leaving the Inkbound Order behind.

For he has found his path at last.

还是说这里的人，其实更想活成猫呢？
en:
Not every cat can survive in a place where the floods come and go.
If you're a newcomer, you'd be wise to find Sesame first.
He's a cat with grand ambitions, a traveler at heart and a notorious rooftop-raider. Though he's just passing through, he knows the ways of the Millennium Crossing like a local.
The people here? Their heads are full of flying goddesses and mythical peach blossom Havens.
It's the kind of place where a cat can truly laze about.
But Sesame, he's not fooled. A Haven? He sniffs at the idea. Life, whether you're a person or a cat, isn't somewhere else. It's right here, right now.
His only real complaint? The rooftops he loves to sunbathe on are always, always crowded with people.
Or maybe... they just secretly wish they were cats.

zh:
丁未年初，契丹入寇东京，烧杀劫掠，死伤无算。南街百坊，侠民一体，共抗契丹。月余，辽主败走，百姓重修坊市，惊见西北老树历经劫火而不死，于枯残之身焕发新芽，以为神异，是谓不死树。

已而刘知远建汉称帝，窃据东京，从官以不死树祥瑞，强驱左近坊民，饰油纸百花于焦枝而修瑞祥园，献于汉帝以贺王祚绵延、千秋不绝。然刘汉二世而斩，岂有百代之功？诚知王朝兴衰非寄于吉凶之物，况乱世之君，安敢亡恐惧之心而作恣意之为乎？

今新宋初立，四海分崩，举国之情未尝优于前汉。上闻瑞祥园旧事，深以为戒，诏令重修此园，易名思危，还于百姓，以明勤修德政、思危怀谨、保国安民之志。

建隆元年七月辛未  立
en:
Thirteen years ago, in the Dingwei year, during a time of chaos, the Khitan army invaded Kaifeng, unleashing fire and slaughter. The people rose to defend their homes, and after a month of bitter fighting, the invaders were repelled. As the city rebuilt, an old tree in the northwest was found scorched by the fires of war, yet miraculously sprouting new leaves. Seeing it as a divine sign of resilience, the people named it the Immortal Tree.
Later, when the usurper Liu Zhiyuan founded his short-lived Han dynasty, his sycophantic court seized upon this story. Claiming the tree as a heavenly omen, they forcibly expelled the local residents and built the Garden of Auspicious Omen, adorning its burnt branches with paper flowers to flatter their emperor.
And yet, what came of it? The Liu Han dynasty collapsed in just two generations. A dynasty's fate is not bound to trinkets and omens. How can a ruler in troubled times dare to cast aside caution for arrogance?
Now, in the first year of Jianlong, with the founding of the Great Song, the realm remains divided. Our Emperor, taking this tale of hubris as a solemn warning, has decreed that the garden be remade. It is renamed the Garden of Vigilance and returned to the people, a testament to his vow to rule with virtue, to remain ever-cautious, and to protect the nation and its people.
Decreed and erected in the seventh month of the first year of the Jianlong era

Shi Zhen, scrambling in the dust for jade pendants, looks like a starving dog.
Weiyang City took away his livelihood, and now he is scrambling for jade pendants given as alms by the Wen family, his enemies.
In the past, he might have hated himself for this, but now he just wants to live.
He has understood. In this world, dignity is nothing but bullshit. Whoever has money can buy human dignity. He has decided. He will abandon dignity. He wants to live, to use this jade pendant to make a comeback. He wants money, lots and lots of money, enough to buy back everything he lost.
After that day, there was one less vendor named Shi Zhen on the street, and one more formidable Shi Zhen in Weiyang City.

女俑身微右转，注视右前方，紧握右拳，左手前伸作控缰状，神情紧张；其身后坐有一猞猁，竖耳瞪眼，前腿直立，后腿屈蹲，十分机警。猞猁乃古代常见的小型助猎猛兽，有其伴身，不难看出女俑所代表的唐代女子们不仅会骑马出行，露髻驰骋，还会参与激烈的骑马狩猎活动。
en:
A Tang dynasty female hunting figurine with a lynx, excavated from the tomb of the Princess of Jinxiang in Xinzhu Township, Baqiao District, Xi'an, and now housed in the Xi'an Museum.
The female rider turns slightly to the right, her gaze fixed ahead to the right. Her right hand is clenched, while her left extends forward as if controlling the reins, her expression tense and focused. Behind her sits a lynx, ears pricked and eyes wide, with its forelegs straight and hind legs tucked beneath it, alert and ready. In antiquity, the lynx was a common small hunting beast. Its presence here suggests that Tang women of the elite not only rode horses and traveled freely with their hair dressed high, but also took part in vigorous mounted hunts.

安雅：


自雅闭门修学以来，日月如梭，转瞬已数月矣。我虽身处乡野，心实系于雅之左右。乱世之中，能得一静谧之地潜心向学，实乃幸事。

其中一#Y沋姓#E男子引人注目，此人五大三粗，身形魁梧，言语间多涉凶险之事。

雅一人在外，切记安全为重。
纸短情长，言不尽意。祈望珍重，盼复。


（情信被撕了一角，导致这份信没有写信人的姓名）
en:
An Ya,

Since you withdrew for your studies, months have passed in the blink of an eye. Though I remain in the quiet countryside, my thoughts never stray far from you. In these turbulent times, to find a peaceful haven for learning is a rare blessing indeed.
Yet the world outside remains restless. Strange visitors have come to our village, their movements cloaked in secrecy.

Of particular note is a man surnamed #YChen#E. He is a hulking, imposing figure, and his speech is steeped in violence and peril.

Please, An Ya, take care of yourself above all. Traveling alone can be dangerous.
Words fall short of all I wish to say. Take heart, and I await your reply with eager hope.

(A corner of this letter has been torn off, leaving the sender's name missing.)

en: The piece has been included in many music scores throughout history, all of which attribute its composition to Sima Xiangru of the Han Dynasty. The earliest known version of the piece is found in the Xilu Tang Music Scores, compiled by Wang Zhi during the Ming Dynasty. However, the most widely circulated version today is found in the Meian Music Scores, which differs from the Xilu Tang Music Scores, suggesting that the original composition has changed over time, making its original form difficult to verify.

玩家的技能大多都可以以卸势应对，破防奇术不仅不会被卸势，在命中处于防御或在释放卸势技能的目标时，反而有更好的效果，但其可以被任意技能打断。玩法中释放卸势会消耗耐力，而处决命中时会回复耐力。

玩家的各类技能（包括奇术和蓄力技）能够打断轻重击，而反过来则不行。解控技能清风霁月可在受击或控制状态下使用，活用可以有效扭转劣势。

移动端与PC端为独立的匹配池。组队参与玩法时，匹配逻辑遵循以下规则：系统将检测队伍内所有成员的设备类型。一旦检测到存在PC端设备，该队伍会被纳入PC端匹配队列。若玩家在移动端匹配成功后出现跨平台顶号等异常行为，则该玩家后续匹配被归入PC端队列。

在限定时间内，率先击败对方全部玩家的一方获胜，若倒计时结束未分胜负，按以下优先级依次判定：
1.存活玩家数量更多的一方获胜；
2.若存活玩家数量相同，则总伤害量更高一方获胜；
3.若总伤害量相同，则总治疗量更高一方获胜。
en:
2v2 Arena is a competitive mode. Match directly or form a 2-player team. In this mode, Arrow usage is capped at 20, teammates cannot be revived, and Healing effects are reduced by 70%. Over time, Damage increases and Healing decreases. 

Most player skills can be countered with Deflection. Guard Break Mystic Skills cannot be deflected and are more effective against targets who are defending or deflecting, but they can be interrupted by any skill. Deflecting consumes Stamina, while landing an Execution restores Stamina. 

Most player Skills (including Mystic Skills and Charged Skills) can interrupt Light and Heavy Attacks, but not vice versa. The CC cleansing skill "Serene Breeze" can be used while under attack or controlled. Use it wisely to turn the tide. 

Mobile and PC have independent matchmaking pools. When teaming up, the system detects device types of all members. If a PC device is detected, the team joins the PC queue. If a player logs in via cross-platform override during a Mobile match, subsequent matches for that player will be assigned to the PC queue. 

Defeat all opponents within the time limit to win. If time expires, the winner is decided by: 
1. More surviving players; 
2. Higher total damage (if survivors equal); 
3. Higher total healing (if damage equal).

...

zh:
狂澜义军自西北而来，驰援王清将军，抵达滹沱河岸者共十五。
那夜，大家就着颓垣村的断壁残垣生了火，喝起了各自揣了一路的那葫酒。康旻不知从哪儿打来了野味，韦青替大家烤熟了下酒。油脂滴火滋滋作响，沈渊师兄却在篝火边舞起了枪，飞舞的枪影宛若游龙。叶轻行和陆凭风靠在悬赏榜下看，魏霄同唐余坐在河边石上拍手叫好，范常安还是那般不安生，急着要同沈渊师兄过上几招……
大帅独自坐在半倾的屋顶，拎着酒葫芦，对着远处沉黑的河面哼起了玉门关外的小曲。
酒巡遍，人声静，凛冽的河风卷着烽火余烬扑面而来。
我们，该动身了。
en:
The Raging Tides volunteers rode from the northwest to reinforce General Wang Qing; only fifteen reached the banks of the Hutuo River.

That night, they built a campfire among the ruins of Ruinstead Village, drinking from the wine gourds they had carried throughout the journey. Kang Min had managed to hunt some wild game, and Wei Qing roasted it over the fire. As the fat dripped into the flames with a sizzle, Senior Brother Shen Yuan began a spear dance, his weapon moving like a soaring dragon. Ye Qingxing and Lu Pingfeng leaned against the bounty board to watch, while Wei Xiao and Tang Yu sat on river stones clapping in approval. Fan Chang'an was as restless as ever, eager to trade a few moves with Shen Yuan.

The Marshal sat alone on a half-collapsed roof, clutching a wine gourd, humming a tune from beyond Jade Gate Pass toward the dark, distant river.

The wine has gone round, the voices have faded. The biting river wind carries the embers of war into our faces.

It is time for us to move.
Li Yihu

中渡桥破，北境离乱。
前曾试送四十余封家书，皆不得至，方知诗家所书“家书抵万金”，字字泣血。
且这许多家书，再不得我的，我们的阿聿代笔了。

书院被围，粮水断绝，突围之械不足，以抽签决人。我与阿聿为墨门弟子，又为院中师长，本意舍生。谁知阿聿知我已有身，竟瞒着将我之名投入签筒。造化弄人，果真中签，令我遭此别离之苦。

因惦念腹中孩子，竟真熬过了那几日寒夜。奈何北境全失，颠沛之中，亦未能……
本当归山，替阿聿尽孝于双亲。奈何经此数难，如遭剜心、作空人，魂消骨立，不能立身。
唯思一事：阿聿之星汉，尚未观录完成。

恕叙儿不孝，往竟阿聿未竟之事，记录山川堪舆，星汉变迁。至多五载，待此间事了，风叙再归山，替阿聿尽孝。
望父亲母亲保重身体，星汉仍在。
en:
Zhongdu Bridge has fallen, and the north is in chaos.
Before this, I tried sending more than forty letters home, yet not one ever arrived. Only now do I understand why the poets say a letter from home is worth ten thousand in gold. Every word of it is written in tears.
And among all those many letters, there will never again be one that Yu writes for me, or for us.

When the academy was besieged, with food and water cut off and too few devices for a breakout, lots were drawn to decide who would go. Yu and I were both Mohist disciples, and teachers at the academy as well. From the first, we had meant to give our lives. Yet when Yu learned that I was with child, he secretly put my name into the lot tube without telling me. Cruel fate had its way, and the lot was truly drawn, leaving me to bear the pain of this parting.

It was only for the sake of the child within me that I managed to endure those bitter nights. And yet, with the whole north lost and my life cast into wandering ruin, I was still unable to...
I ought to have returned to the mountain and fulfilled Yu's filial duty to Father and Mother in his stead. But after all these calamities, my heart feels hollowed out, as though I have become an empty shell. My spirit is spent, my body worn thin, and I can no longer hold myself upright in this world.
Only one thought remains to me. Yu's record of the stars has not yet been finished.

Forgive me for my unfilial heart. I am going now to finish what Yu left unfinished, to record the mountains and rivers, the lay of the land, and the changes in the starry heavens. Give me no more than five years. When all is done, I will return to the mountain and fulfill Yu's duty to you.
Father, Mother, please take care of yourselves. The River of Stars is still there.

zh:
其一 燕子巢
钱江市井的燕子巢不长在屋檐下，长在屋顶上。燕子巢也不是用泥浆草枝做的，却是用布皮包袱和财物做的。
这燕子巢不知道是从何时开始出现的，也不知道是何人所筑，长出来的地方也没有规律。
有时家境颇为殷实的人家屋顶也会长出燕子巢，有时家贫已经无以为继的人家也会失窃。
这筑巢人到底是什么人，又是为了什么总在筑巢，至今仍是个谜团。
钱江人只知若是自家有幸长出一个富贵的燕子巢，便是天降横财，一朝翻身了。于是人心浮动，闹出不少乱子。

其二 风三阵
风三阵原名风七娘，是钱塘码头上的船家出身。待江湖传起名声时，已经没人在乎她的出身，只知道一个名号叫风三阵。
市井人传风三阵有三阵风。
一阵风来，能见千里之外的绣娘如何穿针引线；
二阵风来，能听千里之外的贼匪如何低声密谋；
三阵风来，无论你在何处想找风三阵，只需呼喊其名，说出所求之事与准备的报酬斤两，不出五日，必有消息送达你家。
在杭州西府地界内，想知道什么事、找什么人，总归绕不过风三阵。

其三 义客麒麟生
钱江市井里谁家有难处，第一想连桥会，第二想麒麟生。
麒麟生这个名号取得大，不过不是他自己叫出来的。
他原是个书生，如今也是个书生。吴越以荐举恩荫为先，钱江地界的人祖上无荫，是做不了官的。所以读书的人少，经商的人多，手艺比书卷金贵。
学手艺这件事往往容易闭门造车，要么酒香怕深巷，要么传着传着就没了。
麒麟生原本自称是个义客，其实就是个手艺人之间的掮客。
染布的许家娘子要把染好的布卖出去，麒麟生就替她牵线往裁衣的张家铺子，两方担保谈妥价格，他书生的本事就主要着落在担保和合同文书上。一来二去，立住了一个信誉与公道的名声，人脉如网织起来，能做的事便更多了。
比如东家今年若遭了灾，求助于麒麟生，麒麟生向西家赊借耕牛农具，助东家渡过难关。
西家呢恰有一车货想运往姑苏，麒麟生便寻漕运的弟兄襄助。
漕运弟兄帮了忙，自家也有难，货运船里的锦衣不慎有破，赔偿价格是天价，而东家里有个织娘手艺了得，能补得天衣无缝，便由麒麟生担保将衣服送过去送回来，两厢便宜。
自然事情总不会如此恰好地兜回一圈，只是展示一番麒麟生担保行事，大约就是如此。
他这麒麟之名，就是说各家大小难事遇上他，就如同逢见麒麟一般皆化祥瑞。

其四 过手一杆准
此人本姓已不为人所知，如今姓白，算是白家的门客，据说是白家家主外出施粥时候救回来的。
当日是正月十八，她自己就给自己起了个诨名叫白十八。
连桥会巡视各处，若有缺斤少两的行滥货，都要上报惩处。但上有政策下有对策，市井里能在斤两上做的官司极多且花样翻新，就是用最精细的秤也难免被逃过。这些把戏却是最怕遇见白十八。
白十八的手极准，任何东西到她手里一握一称，一块铁里有几分铜几分泥、一件衣服里悄摸缝进去多少碎布条充作棉布，她都称得明明白白。
做奸的商户试探质疑几次都没得到好处，便干脆认栽，每逢见着她来，就提前把好商品拿出来，等她走了再上假货。
原本白重鹤看她本事高超，必要带着她巡视。如此一来，她觉得白重鹤出行派头太大，便不再跟着家主，只自己低调地晃荡，随处倏隐倏现，叫做奸的商户们防不胜防，只好将真货一贯始终了。

其五 酒馆飞筷
市井的酒馆开得奇，与郎君们常去的酒家是极为不同的。
最明显的不同就在于馆内没有桌椅，人人来了就发一只碗，一文钱一勺酒，刚好够一碗。
来这里的人大多是水陆劳工和走街串巷的脚夫，都是贱卖劳力的人，匆匆进来打一碗，喝完丢下碗就匆匆离开，没空坐下多扒两口饭或多闲谈两句。
酒浊又淡，没味道，将将过个嘴瘾。但市井讨生活的人，本也没有太多钱喝好酒，也没有时间浪费在醉酒上。
讨生活讨得累了来上一碗，酒从嘴里辣过一会儿，暖融融地兜在胃里，堪堪当个安慰，也不妨碍接下去继续做工。
坐馆的掌柜是个五十许的老太，不知道姓名，只知道是从苏州那厢逃难来的，所以被喊作苏老太。
苏老太眼睛极利，谁接了碗没给钱、谁多喝了却少给钱、谁暗自打算抄了碗拿回家去，她都看得清楚。飞一根筷子过去，哪个心怀鬼胎的都得当场跪下。
市井人来人往，不乏功夫好手，却谁也看不清、破不得苏老太的这一手飞筷奇招。

其六 侠名香印
香印之侠名，多传于十几年前。如今知道的人少，忘却的人多。
然雁过留痕，侠过留声，岂能当真尽忘？且以此记。
en:
The First: The Swallow Nest
The swallow nests of the Qianjiang Streets do not grow beneath the eaves, but atop the rooftops. Nor are they built of mud and straw—they are built of cloth bundles and stolen wealth.
No one knows when these swallow nests first began to appear, nor who first built them, nor is there any pattern to where they take root.
Sometimes a well-off household finds a nest sprouting upon its roof; sometimes a family already destitute finds itself robbed all the same.
Who this nest-builder truly is, and why they persist in their building, remains to this day a mystery.
The people of Qianjiang know only this: should their own household be fortunate enough to grow a nest of riches, it is a windfall from heaven, and their fortunes turn overnight. And so hearts grow restless, and no small trouble follows.

The Second: Feng Sanzhen
Feng Sanzhen was once named Feng Qiniang, born to a boatman's family at the Qiantang docks. By the time her name spread through the Jianghu, none cared any longer for her origins—all knew only the name Feng Sanzhen.
The common folk say Feng Sanzhen commands three winds.
When the first wind comes, she may see an embroidery lady a thousand li away, threading her needle;
When the second wind comes, she may hear bandits a thousand li away, plotting in hushed voices;
When the third wind comes, no matter where you stand, should you wish to find Feng Sanzhen, you need only call her name, state your request and the reward you are prepared to offer, and within five days, word shall surely reach your door.
Within the bounds of Hangzhou, whatever one wishes to know, whoever one wishes to find, one cannot avoid passing through Feng Sanzhen.

The Third: Qilin Sage, the Honorbound Guest
When a household in the Qianjiang Streets falls upon hardship, the first thought is of the Connecting Bridge Guild, and the second is of Qilin Sage.
The name Qilin Sage is a grand one, though he never claimed it for himself.
He was once a scholar, and remains one still. In the Wuyue Region, recommendation and hereditary privilege come before all else—those of Qianjiang without ancestral favor cannot enter office. And so few pursue scholarship, and many turn to trade; a craft is worth more than a book of verse here.
Yet learning a craft often means toiling behind closed doors—either the wine's aroma cannot reach the deep alley, or the skill fades away as it passes hand to hand.
Qilin Sage once called himself an honorbound guest, though in truth he was but a broker among craftsmen.
When Lady Xu, the cloth-dyer's wife, wished to sell her dyed cloth, Qilin Sage would connect her to the Zhang family's tailoring shop, guaranteeing both sides and settling a fair price between them—his scholar's talents finding their true use in guarantees and contracts. Little by little, he built a name for trustworthiness and fairness, and as his net of connections grew, so too did what he could accomplish.
Suppose, for instance, one household suffers misfortune this year and seeks Qilin Sage's aid—he might borrow oxen and farming tools on credit from another household to help them through the crisis.
And perhaps that other household has a cart of goods it wishes to send to Gusu—Qilin Sage then seeks out brothers in the freight trade to lend their aid.
And perhaps those freight brothers, having helped, find themselves in trouble too—a fine silk garment aboard their cargo boat has torn, and the price of compensation is dear indeed—but the first household happens to have a weaver girl of great skill, able to mend it without a seam showing, and so Qilin Sage guarantees the garment's safe passage there and back, to the benefit of both sides.
Of course, matters do not always circle back so neatly—this is merely an illustration of how Qilin Sage conducts his guarantees, more or less.
His name, Qilin, speaks to this: that whatever great or small trouble a household meets, encountering him is as fortunate as encountering a qilin itself, turning misfortune to auspiciousness.

The Fourth: A Steady Hand at Weighing
Her original surname is no longer known to any. Now she bears the surname Bai, a retainer of the Bai family, said to have been rescued by the family head himself while distributing porridge to the poor.
That day was the eighteenth of the first month, and so she gave herself the nickname Bai Shiba.
The Connecting Bridge Guild patrols the marketplace, and any merchant found short-weighing or peddling shoddy goods is to be reported and punished. But for every policy above, there is a countermeasure below—the tricks played upon the scales in the marketplace are countless and ever-changing, and even the finest scale can be fooled. Yet these tricks fear nothing more than encountering Bai Shiba.
Bai Shiba's hands are unerringly precise. Whatever object comes into her grip, one weighing tells her all—how many parts copper and how many parts clay lie within a lump of iron, how many scraps of cloth have been secretly stitched into a garment to pass for cotton padding—she can weigh it all out to the last measure.
Corrupt merchants tested and challenged her a few times without gain, and soon simply gave up—whenever they saw her coming, they would bring out their good wares in advance, only switching back to fakes once she had gone.
Bai Chonghe, seeing her extraordinary skill, once insisted on bringing her along on his patrols. But she found his entourage far too conspicuous, and so ceased following the family head, choosing instead to wander alone and unassuming, appearing and vanishing without warning—leaving the corrupt merchants no way to guard against her, and forcing them, in the end, to keep only genuine goods on hand at all times.

The Fifth: The Flying Chopstick of the Tavern
The taverns of the marketplace are a curious sort, quite unlike the wine houses frequented by young gentlemen.
The most obvious difference is that there are no tables or chairs within. Each person who enters is handed a bowl, and for one coin, receives a ladle of wine—just enough to fill it.
Most who come here are laborers of water and land, and porters who wander the streets, all selling their strength cheap. They hurry in, fill a bowl, drink it down, drop the bowl, and hurry off again, with no time to sit and take another bite of rice or exchange idle words.
The wine is cloudy and thin, with little flavor—just enough to satisfy the craving. But those who scrape by in the marketplace have little coin to spend on fine wine, nor time to waste on drunkenness.
When the toil of making a living wearies them, they come for a bowl—the wine burns briefly on the tongue, then settles warm in the belly, a small comfort, and no hindrance to the work that follows.
The keeper of this tavern is an old woman of some fifty years, whose name none know—only that she fled here from Suzhou, and so is called Granny Su.
Granny Su's eyes are sharp indeed. Whoever takes a bowl without paying, whoever drinks more than they paid for, whoever quietly schemes to pocket a bowl and carry it home—she sees it all. A single chopstick flung through the air, and whoever harbored ill intent finds himself kneeling on the spot.
Though the marketplace teems with skilled hands from every corner, none has yet seen through, nor found a counter to, Granny Su's uncanny trick of the flying chopstick.

The Sixth: The Hero's Name
The heroes' names were, for the most part, spread more than a decade ago. Few now remember them; more have let them fade.
And yet, as the wild goose leaves its mark in passing, so too does a hero leave an echo behind—how could it truly be forgotten entirely? And so it is recorded here.

zh:
自沿海径北行，过断崖隘口，可见悠然居隐于桃林深处。院篱斑驳，门户虚掩，闻说昔有隐士居此，今已杳无人迹，惟余空庐寂然。
门外千株桃树绵延如霞，枝头硕果垂垂，朱实盈目，望之令人齿颊生津。

沿海之径多依峭壁而凿，险峻难行，然立崖畔俯瞰，沧波万里尽收眼底。
每至破晓，金乌跃海，云涛尽染，尤称奇观。近海处有幽谷潜藏，潮退则岩洞显露，曲折通幽，暗涛吞吐其间。

沿岸礁石森然罗列，或如巨鳌伏波，或似剑戟插海，嶙峋桀立，怒涛撞击时雪浪崩云。
临此绝险之地，矗碣观海，天地苍茫，逸兴遄飞。
en:
Traveling north along the Cliffside Path and crossing the rift valley pass, one can see the Serenity Cottage hidden deep within a peach grove. The courtyard fence is mottled, the door left slightly ajar. It is said that a hermit once dwelt here, but today, no trace of man remains, leaving only the empty cottage in profound silence.
Outside the gate, thousands of peach trees stretch endlessly like a rosy dawn. Heavy fruits bow the branches, filling the eyes with crimson perfection, causing one's mouth to water at the mere sight.
The coastal path is mostly carved along steep cliffs, treacherous and difficult to tread. Yet, standing at the precipice and looking down, the myriad miles of azure waves are swept into a single glance. Whenever dawn breaks, the Golden Crow leaps from the sea, dyeing the cloudy tides in brilliant hues, a spectacle hailed as a supreme wonder. Near the sea, a hidden valley lies concealed. When the tide recedes, caverns are revealed, twisting and turning into secluded depths where dark currents swallow and spit the waters.
Along the shore, jagged reefs stand in formidable arrays. Some resemble giant turtles resting on the waves, while others look like swords and halberds thrust into the sea, standing tall and unruly. When the furious tides crash against them, the waves shatter into snowy spray that seems to pierce the clouds. Standing upon this perilous edge, gazing at the sea beside the towering stones, before the vastness of heaven and earth, one's free spirit soars upon the wind.
Qi Muzi

zh:
千里烛幼时曾遭遇过一场大水，险些送了命。那时她还是个小女娃，也不怎么记事。她只记得，那一年下了很久很久的雨，最后便是冰冷的水，浸得她骨头直疼。虽然后来被邻家的大叔救下，但千里烛自此也落下了惧水的毛病。
爷娘没少因为这件事呵斥她，但她也只是垂手听着，任打任骂——似乎这样失去反抗便可以为自己赢得片刻的安宁。爷娘刺耳的声音在耳边响起，不知怎地，这些咒骂偶尔会和水声重叠在一起。那难以入耳的腌臜词句也变得模糊。
她摇了摇头，想把这水声从脑海中赶走，却不想这个动作更引得阿爷的怨气。响亮的耳光，让多年的委屈涌上心头。但只一瞬，她便又本能地压抑了心中的波澜，只是顺从地等待狂风暴雨般的辱骂和殴打。而母亲的怀里，幼弟睡得正香。
此刻，水声似乎也变得没那么可怕了。
en:
As a child, Celestial Candle had nearly died in a great flood. She was just a little girl then and didn't remember much. She only recalled that it had rained for a very, very long time that year, and then came the icy water, chilling her bones with pain. Although a neighbor uncle later saved her, Celestial Candle was left with a lasting fear of water. 
Her parents scolded her plenty for it, but she just listened with her hands at her sides, accepting the hitting and the cursing—as if losing the will to resist could buy her a moment's peace. Her parents' shrill voices rang in her ears, and somehow, these curses would occasionally overlap with the sound of water. The unspeakably filthy words became blurred. 
She shook her head, trying to drive the sound of water from her mind, but the motion only incited her father's anger further. A loud slap brought years of grievance surging to her heart. But in an instant, she instinctively suppressed the turmoil inside, simply obediently waiting for the storm of insults and blows. In her mother's arms, her younger brother slept soundly. 
At that moment, the sound of water didn't seem so terrifying anymore.

一小块腐烂的吃食，被馋嘴的孩子弄丢在房间的角落里，刚丢的时候孩子哭闹的整个客栈都兵荒马乱起来。萍水相逢的大人们并不知道这个姓米的孩子大名叫什么，只是亲切地喊他小米仔，小馋猫或者“那个爱吃谷米花的小孩”。大人们不知道，小孩自己也不是很在意。他只要有好听的歌，有跳舞的姐姐逗他玩，以及有姆妈笑着给他的小口袋里装上一把又一把新出炉的谷米花就好。
“父亲，”米嘉荣问他：“你说，你把家弄丢了……弄丢在一个凉州的客栈里？”
“是啊，你说巧不巧。我以为我把它弄丢了，可是近来才想明白，其实我带上了。”
生在长安的孩子不理解父亲在讲什么，就像有一个姓廉的年轻人不理解他祖父口里那些奇怪瑰丽的故事。但这个叫米嘉荣的孩子显然比他父亲小时候要乖得多，所以他只是努力的开动小脑瓜，试图跟上父亲的故事：“那你在客栈里带上的是什么呀？是之前丢了的家吗？”
“是……”小米仔开心的笑了，摇起手鼓，哼起一支熟悉的歌谣。
唱得凉州意外声。但《凉州》唱最好的，是那个爱吃谷米花的小孩。
en:
A small bag of puffed grain, lost and forgotten in a corner. When it first went missing, the child cried so hard he threw the whole inn into a panic.
No one knew the Mi child's full name. People just called him Little Mi, Little Glutton, or the puffed-grain kid. He didn't care. All he wanted was a good song, a dancing big sister to tease him, and his mother smiling as she kept stuffing his little pouch with fresh puffed grain.

"Father, you said you lost our home… at an inn in Liangzhou?" Mi Jiarong asked.
"Yes. I thought I'd lost it. But I've only now realized that I brought it with me."
The Chang'an-born boy didn't understand what his father meant, much like a young man surnamed Lian who couldn't make sense of his grandfather's strange and magnificent stories. Still, he tried his best to follow along.
 "You brought our lost home with you?"
"Yes..." Little Mi beamed, shook his hand drum, and hummed a tune he knew by heart.

They say the best Liangzhou was sung by that puffed-grain kid.

小卫年岁尚小，却有着与年纪不符的"老成"气质。他自诩为"大人"，会特意调整自己的言谈举止，模仿大人的姿态和表达方式，却不自知这种"成熟"只是表面模仿，缺乏生活阅历和深度思考的支撑。他表面装作老成，内心却依然保留着孩童的纯真和好奇心，让人忍俊不禁。比如会被胡杨木做的小动物玩具吸引，自己会偷偷玩过家家的游戏，看到心仪的糖果时眼睛会发亮。
表面上，他认为同村的同龄人过于幼稚，不值得他交往，这导致他在同龄群体中显得格格不入。但实际上，他又非常渴望伙伴们能主动与他搭话，并与他分享那些好玩的、好吃的东西。
en:
Xiao Wei is still young, but he has an "old-fashioned" temperament beyond his years. He prides himself on being an "adult" and deliberately adjusts his words and deeds to imitate the gestures and expressions of adults. However, he doesn't realize that this "maturity" is only superficial imitation, lacking the support of life experience and in-depth thinking. On the surface, he pretends to be sophisticated, but deep down, he still retains the innocence and curiosity of a child, which is amusing. For example, he is attracted to small animal toys made of poplar wood, secretly plays house by himself, and his eyes light up when he sees his favorite candy.

zh:
菩提无数，苦海无涯。璧泉山以东，有沼泽数十里，名曰“菩提苦海”。相传唐时玄奘法师东传佛法，于此地开筳讲经，永福禅师由此得悟，手栽菩提树一株，即为苦海边的原初菩提根，今已亭亭如盖。
至前朝显德年间，佛子妙善率众弟子于苦海深处建罪业塔，囚罪人百余，诸僧于塔外敲鼓鸣钟，为诸罪人洗涤业障。夜漏尽，钟鸣即起，昼漏尽，鼓声则息。苦海无边，回头是岸，晨钟暮鼓，向无止境。后妙善禅师不知所踪，诸罪人破塔而出，苦海沦为人间惨境。罪业塔经此浩劫，唯余断壁残垣。
近年时有土人闻苦海深处哀嚎隐隐，言其为昔日陨身塔中冤魂作祟，疑为谬传。
en:
East of Jadebrook Mountain lies a vast swamp known by a name of profound paradox: the Bodhi Sea. A sea of suffering, yet a place of enlightenment.
Legend claims its hopeful beginning traces back to the Tang Dynasty, when the great monk Xuanzang preached here. Inspired, a master named Yongfu attained enlightenment and planted a single Bodhi sapling by the water's edge. That tree now stands majestic, its canopy a vast, sheltering pavilion—a lone symbol of the grace that once was.
But this grace soured. During the Xiande era, the zealous monk Miaoshan led his followers into the swamp's heart. There, they built the Karma Pagoda and imprisoned a hundred sinners within. Guided by the tenet, "The sea of suffering is boundless, yet repentance is the shore," the monks outside began a ceaseless vigil. Morning bells and evening drums echoed across the waters, an unending ritual meant to cleanse the prisoners' souls.
Then, Master Miaoshan vanished. The prisoners, their penance unfinished, shattered the pagoda's walls. The Bodhi Sea, once a place of potential salvation, devolved into a hell on earth. Of the great pagoda, only shattered ruins remain.
To this day, locals whisper of faint, sorrowful wails drifting from the swamp's depths. They attribute the sounds to the vengeful spirits of those who perished in the tower, though such tales are likely just superstition.

zh:
《玉篇》有云，“骁勇也。”骠，马行疾貌，又指毛色中夹杂点点斑纹。西南矮脚中有此纹理者，为赤骠。
《华阳国志·南中志》记载：“长老传言，滇池有神马，或交焉，即生骏驹，俗称称之曰‘滇池驹’，日行五百里。”唐宋时期，《蛮书》又云：“马出越赕山东面一带……尾高，尤善驰骤，日行数百里。……腾冲及申赕亦出马，次赕，滇池尤佳。”《新唐书·南诏传》亦载：“越赕之西有荐草，产善马，世称‘越赕骏’。始生若羔，岁中，细莎縻之，饮以米渖，七年可御，日驰数百里。”滇马即为矮脚马，因产于滇池，故名“西南矮脚”。
西南矮脚体格极小，四肢较细，颈短头直，眼大额广，蹄小而质坚，以耐力见长，乘、挽、驮均可，为西南最常见的马种。
en:
The Jade Chapters describes the Biao horse as "fierce and brave," known for its speed and the small, speckled spots marking its coat. Among the Southwestern Ponies, those with this distinct red-dappled pattern are called Chibiao.
Legends from the Huayang Chorography tell of a divine steed that once rose from Dianchi Lake. Its offspring, known as "Dianchi Foals," were said to travel five hundred li a day. Later, during the Tang and Song dynasties, texts like the Book of the Man and the New Book of Tang praised the swift, high-tailed horses bred on the lush grasslands of the region, famed as "Yuetan Steeds." These Dian Horses, named for their origin near Dianchi Lake, are also known as Southwestern Ponies.
Small in stature, they have fine limbs, a short neck, a broad forehead, and firm, compact hooves. Prized for their endurance, they are suited for riding, pulling, and carrying loads, making them the most common breed in the southwest.

en:
To be honest, no one ever imagined this day would arrive—nor did we expect it to come so swiftly and suddenly! And when it finally did, we realized how unpredictable fate is and how insignificant all things are! 
Yesterday morning, the Evercare Clinic received an emergency call—three Giant Geese, our daily companions, had suddenly collapsed, unconscious! Our in-house Goose Whisperer immediately rushed to the scene and interviewed an eyewitness goose. According to its account, at noon, the geese in question were wandering outside when they noticed billowing smoke ahead, carrying a tantalizing aroma... They "honked-honked-honked" their way toward it, only to find two Giant Geese sprawled over their nest, their white feathers scorched, revealing a fully cooked Egg! Overwhelmed, the witness goose fainted on the spot... 
Fortunately, timely intervention ensured no serious harm. The physician remarked that while stealing eggs to hatch is shameful, nest placement requires caution. The root cause of the geese's successive collapses was the scorching heat—the sweltering summer has arrived, and both humans and geese must prioritize heatstroke prevention. 
In the coming days, our reporters will interview several locals to share summer survival tips, ensuring not a single goose or egg is neglected! Stay tuned for tomorrow's update!

He traveled far and wide, and when he passed through Kaifeng, he was so taken by its scenery that he decided to stay awhile. After helping to suppress the rebellion led by Li Jun and Li Zhongjin, Li Chongju was appointed Commissioner of Imperial Ceremonial Affairs and was granted the Li family estate as a reward. Twelve years later, the two old friends crossed paths again on the streets of Kaifeng. There was so much left unspoken between them, but neither knew how to begin. At last, Li Chongju broke the silence and invited Ma Sizhong over. Without hesitation, Ma Sizhong agreed. Tensions between the civil and military officials in the city were at an all-time high. After Ma Sizhong moved in, he often urged Li Chongju not to pick sides too hastily. This time, instead of arguing like before, the two remained calm. Li Chongju found himself quietly weighing Ma Sizhong's advice, his determination starting to waver.

沿着通往飞天城的小路，你拾得一只坠落的纸鸢。纸鸢早已褪色破损，却在尾翼上有几个小字，莫非是纸鸢的主人？
⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛
这只残破的纸鸢是否也曾穿云破雾？它也曾与白云和苍鹰一同高飞吗？它从空中坠落时也曾奋力振翅吗？
飞鸢应该属于天空，只要风还在吹，它总有再起飞之时。
en:
Though Skyward City lies in ruins, the skeletal remains of the colossal Peng still whisper of its former glory. How could a Skyward City of such scale crumble overnight? How have its ruins remained suspended, defying gravity and time alike, all these years?
Along the narrow path to Skyward City, you chance upon a fallen kite. Though faded and frayed, a few characters grace its tail. Could they be the owner's name?

Did this tattered kite once pierce the clouds and part the mists? Did it once soar alongside the drifting clouds and the noble hawks? Did it beat its wings in a final, frantic struggle as it plunged from the heavens?
A kite's destiny lies with the sky; as long as the winds breathe, it shall have its moment to soar once more.

With bare hands, I carve my path through life and death. With my own body, I leap beyond right and wrong. Justice and truth, I will decide.

The second is consumed by lust: a lecherous fiend who preys on decent folk by the foulest tricks. The third is driven by greed: running the Golden Toad Manor, a place that bleeds men dry. The fourth is ruled by wrath: his temper so violent that the slightest spark sets him ablaze.
Hu Bushuo claims all this to be a fanciful tale from a dream, but you can't have smoke without fire. The jianghu is a perilous place, and if you do meet these four, watch your back.

zh:
《说文解字》有云：“驳，马色不纯。从马，爻声。”吐谷浑马中杂而不纯者，为青驳。
相传秦时甘陇一带产良马，时称“秦马”。西汉景帝年间，在西北边郡设马苑，养秦马万千，后有吐谷浑人驻牧。《隋书》有云：“吐谷浑有青海，中有小山。其俗至动辄方牝马与其上，言其龙种。尝得波斯草马放入海，因生骢驹，日行千里。”书中所云骢驹即为“吐谷浑马”。
吐谷浑马骨充肌丰，体躯舒展，健而有力，温顺易驯。喜群居，好游走，群马中必有公马为首。耳聪目明，性机敏，记心强，同类相惜，认主不忘。可乘骑，可轻挽，为中原最常见的马种。
en:
The Shuowen Jiezi explains: "The character bo means a horse of impure color." Among the Tuyuhun horses, those with such an uneven, bluish-mottled coat were called Qingbo, or Azure Piebalds.
Legends say the Ganlong region produced fine "Qin Horses" as early as the Qin Dynasty. Later, the Tuyuhun people settled there to graze their herds. According to the Book of Sui, a myth tells of a Persian stallion that bred with a local mare near Qinghai Lake, producing a Cong colt that could run a thousand li a day. This legendary colt became known as the Tuyuhun Horse.
Muscular and well-proportioned, the Tuyuhun Horse is strong yet gentle and easy to train. These horses are highly social, moving in herds led by a dominant stallion. With keen ears and sharp eyes, they are intelligent, alert, and fiercely loyal to both their kind and their master. Suited for riding and light draft work, they became one of the most common breeds in the Central Plains.

你知道他一向不喜争辩，便走上前去替他解围：
#Y【山？】说到山，我突然想到三十六计中曾言，一、二、山……冯大哥，我们快跑！#E
众人听罢皆为之一怔，趁他们尚在回味中，你一口气把冯大哥拉出了人群。气息平复后，你左看右看，总觉得冯大哥有了些变化，却说不上来。适逢一阵强风吹来，冯大哥摸了摸自己的脑袋——
好消息是，冯大哥虽潜心科研，但头发依旧很茂密！
坏消息是，冯大哥的帽子被落在亭子里了……
en:
At Confluence Gazebo, they recount history; at the Disputation Platform, they debate the ages. With storms brewing of late, the debate between Expansion and Seclusion has become the center of daily discourse.
Accustomed to such scenes, you are passing the place when you spot a familiar figure surrounded by a clamoring crowd. To the left, voices clamor to seal the gate; to the right, they shout to open it. Caught in the middle, Feng is in a total bind.
Knowing his distaste for disputes, you step forward to bail him out:
#Y[Mountains?] Speaking of mountains... it reminds me of the Thirty-Six Stratagems: One, two, and... Run Feng, let's get out of here!#E
The crowd falls into a stunned silence. Seizing the moment while they reflect, you pull Feng through the throng in one swift motion. Once your breath is caught, you look him up and down. Something about Feng seems different, though you can't quite put your finger on it. Just then, a gust of wind sweeps by. Feng instinctively feels his head...
The good news: despite his devotion to research, Feng's hair remains thick and lush!
The bad news: his hat was left behind in Confluence Gazebo...

你知道他一向不喜争辩，便走上前去替他解围：
#Y【开山好！】墨门讲究济世利民，如今山外形势变幻莫测，墨门子弟自当义不容辞！#E
众人听罢皆为之一怔，趁他们尚在回味中，你一口气把冯大哥拉出了人群。气息平复后，你左看右看，总觉得冯大哥有了些变化，却说不上来。适逢一阵强风吹来，冯大哥摸了摸自己的脑袋——
好消息是，冯大哥虽潜心科研，但头发依旧很茂密！
坏消息是，冯大哥的帽子被落在亭子里了……
en:
At Confluence Gazebo, they recount history; at the Disputation Platform, they debate the ages. With storms brewing of late, the debate between Expansion and Seclusion has become the center of daily discourse.
Accustomed to such scenes, you are passing the place when you spot a familiar figure surrounded by a clamoring crowd. To the left, voices clamor to seal the gate; to the right, they shout to open it. Caught in the middle, Feng is in a total bind.
Knowing his distaste for disputes, you step forward to bail him out:
#Y[Expansion!] Mohism values the welfare of the people. With the world in flux, it is our duty to serve the benefit of all!#E
The crowd falls into a stunned silence. Seizing the moment while they reflect, you pull Feng through the throng in one swift motion. Once your breath is caught, you look him up and down. Something about Feng seems different, though you can't quite put your finger on it. Just then, a gust of wind sweeps by. Feng instinctively feels his head...
The good news: despite his devotion to research, Feng's hair remains thick and lush!
The bad news: his hat was left behind in Confluence Gazebo...

他踉跄着闯入密林水泽，寒潭的凉意才让中烧的怒火慢慢平息。
他这才惊觉，师父的素白头纱竟在缠斗间挂在了自己身上。
是被之前被他不小心扯坏，用缝伤口的针法勉强缝好的旧纱，还是孙愿攒了数月银钱送给师父的新纱？
正怔忡间，齐腰深的流水将头纱卷走，瞬间没了踪影。

偏执心起，明知师父不可能再穿戴他染指之物，可他偏想弄清楚。
他纵身扎入寒潭，俯身在水底摸索，指尖触到一抹莹白，可几近窒息也没能将它捞起。
待破水而出，他才发现，那是月亮在水中的倒影。
en:
He stumbled into the dense marshlands, the frigid water finally cooling his raging fury.
Only then did he notice that his Master's pure white veil had snagged on his clothes during their struggle.
Was it the old one he had accidentally torn and clumsily patched up like a stitched wound, or the new one Sun Yuan had spent months saving up to buy for her? As he stood there dazedly, the waist-deep current swept the veil away, swallowing it in an instant.

A sudden obsession took hold of him. He knew his Master would never again wear something he had touched, yet he had to know which veil it was.
Plunging into the freezing pool, he blindly searched the bottom. His fingertips brushed against a pale shimmer, but even as he ran out of breath, he couldn't grasp it. 
Bursting through the surface for air, he finally realized what it was—just the reflection of the moon.

en:
Only a solitary flying bird is seen, its cry echoing a thousand li.
It was a cherished object, crafted by a craftsman named Brant.
Now it lies broken on the ground, wilting.
When did it fall from the sky?
Was it when the fire burned through its flesh and bone? Or when the craftsman's blood soaked its feathers?
Did it die with that solitary, thousand-li cry?
It only remembers that in that final moment of falling, ten thousand Wooden Eagles rose beside it.

东岳有危崖，壁削千尺。屋舍缘岩而结，檐牙相钩。如蜂房蚁垤，连缀不绝，此降龙寨也。
昔时悍匪盘踞，众匪首取诨名“浪里黑龙”，谋据青州，百姓患之。后有祝氏二女，以擒龙之势，逐匪出青州。余众骇服，推之为寨主，寨由是更名“降龙”。自此，寨中虽仍是那班亡命，却渐有生业。众匪于山阴辟渔场，数年之间，仓廪稍实，人烟日稠。
近日有渔人迷舟，误近山脚，但闻锣鼓喧天，喝彩声如潮涌，莫知其庆何事。
未几，风声四起，大寨主独身离寨，去向杳然，小寨主年岁尚轻，心性未定。
一寨之柱，去一留一。江湖浪起，恐非久安之兆矣。
en:
At the Eastern Peak there stands a perilous cliff, its face sheer for a thousand feet. Dwellings are lashed together along the rock face, eaves hooking into eaves, like honeycombs and ant-mounds, strung together without end. This is the Dragonfall Camp.
In former days, bandits held the place in their grip. Their chiefs took the epithet "Black Dragons of the Waves" and schemed to seize Qingzhou, to the great suffering of its commoners. Then came two women of the Zhu clan, who with the momentum of dragon-tamers drove most bandits from Qingzhou. The rest were struck with awe and submitted, naming the Zhu sisters their Chiefs, and so the camp was renamed "Dragonfall." From that day forth, though the camp remained home to that same band of desperate souls, they gradually found honest livelihoods. The bandits opened fisheries on the shaded side of the mountain, and within a few years the granaries grew somewhat full, and the smoke of hearths grew denser day by day.
Not long ago, a fisherman lost his way and drew near the foot of the mountain by accident. He heard only the gongs and drums thundering loud, and waves of applause like surging tides, yet he knew not what occasion was being celebrated.
Soon after, rumors began to stir: the Elder Chief had left the camp alone, her whereabouts unknown; the Younger Chief was still of tender years, her temperament unsettled.
Of the two pillars of the camp, one has gone and one remains. The waves of the Jianghu are rising... this bodes ill for any lasting peace.

zh:
【既夕礼第十三】

既夕哭，请启期，告于宾。
夙兴，设盥于祖庙门外。陈鼎皆如殡，东方之馔亦如之。夷床馔于阶间。
二烛俟于殡门外。丈夫髽，散带垂，即位如初。妇人不哭。主人拜宾，入，即位，袒。商祝免袒，执功布入，升自西阶，尽阶，不升堂。声三，启三，命哭。烛入。祝降，与夏祝交于阶下。取铭置于重。踊无算。商祝拂柩用功布，幠用夷衾。
迁于祖，用轴。重先，奠从，烛从，柩从，烛从，主人从。升自西阶。奠俟于下，东面北上。主人从升，妇人升，东面。众主人东即位。正柩于两楹间，用夷床。主人柩东，西面。置重如初。席升设于柩西。奠设如初，巾之，升降自西阶。主人踊无算，降，拜宾，即位，踊，袭。主妇及亲者由足，西面。
荐车，直东荣，北輈。质明，灭烛。彻者升自阼阶，降自西阶。乃奠如初，升降自西阶。主人要节而踊。荐马，缨三就，入门，北面，交辔，圉人夹牵之。御者执策立于马后。哭成踊，右还，出。宾出，主人送于门外。
有司请祖期。曰：“日侧。”主人入，袒。乃载，踊无算。卒束。袭。降奠，当前束。商祝饰柩，一池，纽前<赤巠>后缁，齐三采，无贝。设披。属引。
陈明器于乘车之西。折，横覆之。抗木，横三，缩二。加抗席三。加茵，用疏布，缁翦，有幅，亦缩二横三。器西南上，綪。茵。苞二。筲三，黍，稷，麦。瓮三，醯，醢，屑。幂用疏布。甒二，醴，酒。幂用功布。皆木桁，久之。用器：弓矢，耒耜，两敦，两杅，槃，匜。匜实于槃中，南流。无祭器。有燕乐器可也。役器，甲，胄，干，笮。燕器，杖，笠，翣。
彻奠，巾席俟于西方。主人要节而踊，袒。商祝御柩，乃祖。踊，袭，少南，当前束。妇人降，即位于阶间。祖，还车不还器。祝取铭，置于茵。二人还重，左还。布席，乃奠如初，主人要节而踊。荐马如初。宾出。主人送，有司请葬期。入，复位。
公賵玄纁束，马两。摈者出请，入告。主人释杖，迎于庙门外，不哭。先入门右，北面，及众主人袒。马入设。宾奉币，由马西当前辂，北面致命。主人哭，拜稽颡，成踊。宾奠币于栈左服，出。宰由主人之北，举币以东。士受马以出。主人送于外门外，拜，袭，入复位，杖。
……
en:
【The Thirteenth Chapter of the Evening Funeral Rites】

After the evening mourning, the date for the encoffining was requested and announced to the guests.
Rising early, basins were set up outside the gate of the ancestral temple. The tripods were arranged as at the funeral, and the offerings in the eastern chamber were likewise prepared. The mourning bed was placed between the steps.
Two torches were kept ready outside the funeral gate. The men wore mourning headbands with loose sash ends hanging down, and took their positions as before. The women did not wail. The host bowed to the guests, entered, took his position, and bared his arms. The Shang priest, with headpiece removed and arms bared, entered holding the ceremonial cloth, ascending by the western steps. When he reached the top of the steps, he did not ascend into the hall. He called out three times, then opened the coffin three times, and commanded the wailing to begin. The torches were brought in. The priest descended and met the Xia priest at the foot of the steps. He took the inscription tablet and placed it on the funeral stand. They leaped without counting. The Shang priest brushed the coffin with the ceremonial cloth and covered it with the mourning quilt.
The coffin was moved to the ancestral temple using rollers. The funeral stand went first, followed by the offerings, then the torches, then the coffin, then more torches, and the host followed. They ascended by the western steps. The offerings waited below, facing east with the northernmost position highest. The host ascended following the coffin, and the women ascended and stood facing east. The other relatives took their positions on the east. The coffin was straightened between the two pillars using the mourning bed. The host stood east of the coffin, facing west. The funeral stand was placed as before. The mat was brought up and laid west of the coffin. The offerings were set out as before, covered with cloth, and ascended and descended by the western steps. The host leaped without counting, descended, bowed to the guests, took his position, leaped, and put on his clothes. The host's wife and close relatives passed by the foot of the coffin and stood facing west.
The carriage was brought forward, aligned with the eastern eave, with the shaft pointing north. At dawn, the torches were extinguished. The attendants ascended by the eastern steps and descended by the western steps. Then the offerings were set out as before, ascending and descending by the western steps. The host leaped at the appropriate moments. The horses were brought in, with tassels of three strands, entering the gate, facing north, with crossed reins, led by the grooms on either side. The driver stood behind the horses holding the whip. Wailing and leaping were completed, then they turned right and went out. The guests departed, and the host escorted them outside the gate.
The officer requested the date for the ancestral sacrifice. The host said, "When the sun declines." The host entered and bared his arms. Then the coffin was loaded, and they leaped without counting. When the binding was complete, he put on his clothes. The offerings were lowered and placed before the binding. The Shang priest adorned the coffin with a pool, with red cords at the front and black at the back, and tassels of three colors without shells. The straps were attached, and the ropes were connected.
The funerary objects were displayed west of the carriage. The frame was laid across. The crossbars were three horizontally and two vertically. Three mats were added on top. The covering cloth was added, made of coarse fabric, black and trimmed, with width, also two vertical and three horizontal. The vessels were arranged from the southwest corner upward, in a zigzag pattern. The mats. Two bundles of offerings. Three baskets: millet, glutinous millet, and wheat. Three jars: vinegar, meat sauce, and grain flour. Covered with coarse cloth. Two vats: sweet wine and wine. Covered with ceremonial cloth. All were placed on wooden stands and secured. Utensils for use: bow and arrows, plow and hoe, two round vessels, two ladles, a basin, and a ewer. The ewer was placed in the basin with its spout facing south. No sacrificial vessels. It was permissible to have instruments for entertainment. Military equipment: armor, helmets, shields, and quivers. Leisure items: staff, straw hat, and fan.
The offerings were removed, and the cloth and mat were kept ready in the west. The host leaped at the appropriate moments and bared his arms. The Shang priest led the coffin, and the ancestral sacrifice began. They leaped, put on clothes, moved slightly south, and stood before the binding. The women descended and took their positions between the steps. For the ancestral sacrifice, the carriage was turned but not the vessels. The priest took the inscription and placed it on the covering cloth. Two men turned the funeral stand to the left. The mat was spread, and the offerings were set out as before, with the host leaping at the appropriate moments. The horses were presented as before. The guests departed. The host escorted them out, and the officer requested the burial date. The host entered and returned to his position.
The duke sent gifts of dark and crimson silk, two bolts, and two horses. The usher went out to inquire, then entered to announce. The host set down his staff, went out to meet them outside the temple gate, without wailing. He first entered through the right side of the gate, facing north, and bared his arms along with the other relatives. The horses were brought in and set down. The guest, holding the silk, came from the west of the horses, stood before the front shaft, and delivered the message facing north. The host wailed, bowed with his head to the ground, and leaped. The guest placed the silk on the left side of the carriage and went out. The steward, passing north of the host, picked up the silk and went east. The officer received the horses and led them out. The host escorted them outside the outer gate, bowed, put on his clothes, entered, and returned to his position with his staff.
……

A drunken man attempts to make his way to the Phantoms' Hollow for some sour soup

With no other choice, you resolve to fetch the sour soup for him.

zh:
长安，长安。
月兔很久没听到人提起过这个名字了。
女子消失之后，它在凉州城里团团转了几天，接着，它开始朝着月亮奔跑。
它知道月亮很远很远，长安也很远很远。月亮是不会消失的，长安也是不会消失的，只要它一直跑下去，总有一天会跑到月亮里，跑回长安去，那时，是不是也能见到她呢？
它终究没有跑到月亮里，它精疲力竭地倒在另一个女子腿边。女子的手抚摸着它的背，它在她手心里渐渐热了。
月亮是冷的，长安也是冷的。每一次，每一次温暖它的，都是一双女子的手。
en:
Chang'an, Chang'an. 
Moon Rabbit hadn't heard the name spoken in what felt like an eternity. 
After the woman vanished, it wandered restlessly through the streets of Liangzhou for days. Then it began to run—toward the moon. 
It knew the moon was distant—Chang'an even more so. Yet neither vanished. If it kept running, one day it would reach the moon, return to Chang'an, and maybe see her again. 
But it never made it to the moon. Exhausted, it finally collapsed at the feet of another woman. Her gentle hand brushed its back, and warmth slowly bloomed within its cold body. 
The moon is cold, and so is Chang'an. Yet every time warmth found it, it came through the touch of a woman's hand.

zh:
建安十三年，曹操率军二十万众顺江而下。周瑜率精军三万沿江上至夏口，联合屯驻樊口的刘备军一起溯长江西进，与曹军相遇在赤壁。周瑜采纳部将黄盖之议用火攻，设计诈降，命其率小战船十艘，上装柴草，灌以膏油，假称投降，向北岸而进，至离曹营二里之处时，各船一齐点火，然后借助风势，直向曹军冲去，曹军大败，舟船被烧，延及岸上曹营而伤亡惨重，曹操又下令将剩余的曹军舟船都予以烧毁，然后撤退。后人称其为：肯得计，烽狂行旗嘶，魏卧吴师！
今日你若喂我五十，来日，我必报以聚宝生资！
en:
In the 13th year of Jian'an, Cao Cao led two hundred thousand troops down the river. Zhou Yu led thirty thousand elite troops up to Xiakou, joining Liu Bei's forces at Fankou to advance west. They met Cao's army at Red Cliff. Zhou Yu adopted Huang Gai's plan of fire attack and a ruse of surrender. Huang Gai led ten warships filled with firewood and oil, pretending to surrender. Two miles from Cao's camp, the ships were lit and driven by the wind into Cao's fleet. Cao's army was utterly defeated; ships were burned, and the fire spread to the camps on the shore, causing heavy casualties. Cao Cao ordered the remaining ships burned and retreated. Later generations called it: The Keen Flame Strategy, the Banner of the Fierce Wind, the Wei Falls to the Wu!

zh:
第一页
夫，走，两年。今，识字，记。

第二页
今日识“家、安、月、霞、归……”，家，安好，你，可好？

第十五页
今日又来征兵，张婶家的娃也去了。识的字多了，村里的人少了。

第二十四页
今日又同霞儿一道习字，阿公教了菜微。
菜微菜微，曰归曰归。霞儿还说我写错了。女儿大了，你何时归。

第四十五页
芦草黄了，又到冬天。今早下河捞鱼，听到有人哭喊，救起一对落水的母女。

第五十页
那女娃烧了三天了，阿公找到了些草药，希望能好。我问女娃娘，她们从哪来。她不肯说。
孤儿寡母的，多半有苦衷，只是她俩的长相……

第五十七页
女娃她娘叫梨朵。原来她不是契丹人，是逃出来的西人。西人，是从西边来的吗？如今北边西边都在打仗……我问她为什么逃，她又不说了。

第六十八页
天越来越冷了，阿公也患了咳疾，梨朵阿妹送了些草药来，她识字虽慢，但识草药倒有一手，我送了些鱼给她。（似拿不住笔，字有些歪斜）

第七十页
原来奚人的奚是这么写。
和梨朵阿妹同做绣片，阿妹绣工好，学些繁复花样也快，还会不少异族样式。咱们商量着多攒些拿出去换点嚼用。
今日才知，阿妹逃来这里，原是为找她汉子。她汉子被契丹强征了兵，才离家没多久，便传来消息，说他是怂包软蛋当了逃兵，又有说是违了军纪被处死了。她不信汉子已死，便出来找，天大地大的，去哪找呢……她一路走，一路躲，竟又发现自己有了身孕。再带着身子往南，走到咱们这儿，孩子都几岁了……哎，如今也回不去了。爹说若咱也降了，今日的奚人便是明日的咱们……我近来总有些心悸，不知你可安好。（似拿不住笔，字更加歪歪扭扭）

第七十二页
梨朵阿妹……来看我……让我给她女儿起个名……我说……就叫芦花吧……（写字之人已握不住笔，字更加难以辨认）

最后一页
河冻上……鱼没了……得出去……换粮……

（手记就到这里，其后再无更多）
en:
First Page
Husband gone two years.
Now know some words. Write this.

Second Page
Today learned "home, safe, Yue, Xia, return"...
Home safe. You well?

Fifteenth Page
They came for more soldiers again today. Even Aunt Zhang's boy was taken.
Know more words now. Fewer people in the village now.

Twenty-Fourth Page
Today Xia'er and I wrote again. Father taught Caiwei.
Picking ferns... going home... Xia'er said I wrote it wrong. Daughter grown now. When will you come home?

Forty-Fifth Page
The reeds are yellow. Winter is here again.
This morning I went to the river to catch fish and heard people crying out. I pulled a mother and daughter from the water.

Fiftieth Page
That little girl has burned with fever three days now. Father found some herbs. I hope she lives.
I asked the girl's mother where they came from. She would not say.
A mother and child alone must have troubles of their own. Only... the way they look...

Fifty-Seventh Page
The girl's mother is called Liduo. So she is not Khitan after all, but Xi who escaped.
Xi... is that from the west?
There is war now in the north and in the west too... I asked why she fled, and again she would not speak.

Sixty-Eighth Page
The weather grows colder by the day. Father has taken a cough too. Liduo brought some herbs. She is slow with letters, but very good with herbs. I gave her some fish in return.
(The hand is unsteady here, and the characters slant.)

Seventieth Page
So this is how the Xi in Xi people is written.
Today I did embroidery with Liduo. Her needlework is good, and she learns fine patterns quickly. She also knows many designs from other peoples. We talked of saving up more pieces to trade for a little food and spending money.
Only today did I learn that she came here looking for her husband. He was taken by the Khitans and forced into the army. Not long after he left home, word came back that he was a coward and a weakling who had deserted. Others said he had broken military law and been put to death. She would not believe he was dead, so she went looking for him. But with the world so vast, where would she go? She kept walking, hiding as she went, and only then found she was with child. Even so, she kept heading south. By the time she reached our place, the child was already several years old... Ah, and now there is no going back. Father says that if we surrender too, then what the Xi are today, we will be tomorrow... Lately my heart has often been uneasy. I wonder whether you are safe.
(The hand grows weaker here, the writing more twisted and uneven.)

Seventy-Second Page
Liduo... came to see me... asked me to name her daughter... I said... call her Luhua...
(The writer can no longer hold the brush. The characters are harder still to make out.)

Last Page
River frozen... no fish... must go out... trade for grain...

(That is where the notebook ends. Nothing more follows.)

zh:
这是小耳朵第六次离家出走。
虽然主人收养了它，但它还是怀念以前的日子，想当只自由自在的野狗。
日复一日地吃饭、看门、陪主人可不是它的志向。它要去看得最远的地方，追蝴蝶，扑麻雀，品野果，闻风带来的各种香。
可是......这个草丛到底有什么陷阱！为什么每次刚走到这儿，狗肚子就会咕咕作响，明明每次都吃了一大块肉才出门。
小耳朵这样想着，又一次垂头丧气地回了家。
en:
This is Little Ears's sixth time running away.
His owner took him in, sure, but he misses the old days. He wants to be a free dog again.
Eating, guarding the house, keeping his owner company, day after day? Not for him. He wants to go to the farthest place he can see, chase butterflies, pounce on sparrows, taste wild berries, and follow whatever scents the wind brings.
But... is this patch of grass a trap? Every time he gets there, his stomach starts growling. And he definitely ate a huge meal before leaving.
Little Ears sighs, and, for the sixth time, trudges back home.

【昏义第四十四】

昏礼者，将合二姓之好，上以事宗庙，而下以继后世也。故君子重之。是以昏礼纳采、问名、纳吉、纳征、请期，皆主人筵几于庙，而拜迎于门外，入，揖让而升，听命于庙，所以敬慎重正昏礼也。
父亲醮子，而命之迎，男先于女也。子承命以迎，主人筵几于庙，而拜迎于门外。婿执雁入，揖让升堂，再拜奠雁，盖亲受之于父母也。降，出御妇车，而婿授绥，御轮三周。先俟于门外，妇至，婿揖妇以入，共牢而食，合卺而酳，所以合体同尊卑以亲之也。
敬慎重正而后亲之，礼之大体，而所以成男女之别，而立夫妇之义也。男女有别，而后夫妇有义；夫妇有义，而后父子有亲；父子有亲，而后君臣有正。故曰：昏礼者，礼之本也。
夫礼始于冠，本于昏，重于丧祭，尊于朝聘，和于射乡--此礼之大体也。
夙兴，妇沐浴以俟见；质明，赞见妇于舅姑，执笲、枣、栗、段修以见，赞醴妇，妇祭脯醢，祭醴，成妇礼也。舅姑入室，妇以特豚馈，
en:
【Meaning of the Wedding Ceremony, Section 44】

The wedding ceremony is meant to unite the goodwill of two families, serving above to honor the ancestral temple and below to continue posterity. Therefore, the gentleman regards it with great importance. Thus, in the wedding ceremony, from the proposal, inquiry of the bride's name, divination of auspiciousness, presentation of betrothal gifts, and fixing of the date, the host always prepares mats and tables in the ancestral temple, welcomes the guest outside the gate, and upon entering, bows and yields as they ascend, receiving instructions in the temple—this is to show reverence, caution, and correctness in the wedding ceremony.
The father gives a toast to his son and instructs him to go and welcome the bride, for the man takes precedence over the woman. The son receives the instruction and goes to welcome her. The host prepares mats and tables in the ancestral temple and welcomes the guest outside the gate. The groom enters carrying a wild goose, bows and yields as he ascends the hall, bows twice, and presents the wild goose—this signifies receiving the bride personally from her parents. He descends, goes out, and drives the bride's carriage, and the groom hands her the mounting strap, driving the wheels around three times. He waits outside the gate beforehand; when the bride arrives, the groom bows to her and leads her in. They share a meal together, and drink from the split gourd, symbolizing union of bodies and equality of status to show intimacy.
After showing reverence, caution, and correctness, they then become intimate—this is the great essence of ritual, and it is how the distinction between man and woman is established, and the righteousness between husband and wife is defined. When there is distinction between man and woman, then there is righteousness between husband and wife; when there is righteousness between husband and wife, then there is affection between father and son; when there is affection between father and son, then there is correctness between ruler and minister. Hence it is said: The wedding ceremony is the foundation of ritual.
Now, ritual begins with the capping ceremony, is founded on the wedding ceremony, is most weighty in mourning and sacrifice, is honored in court audiences and diplomatic visits, and is harmonized in archery and district gatherings—these are the great essentials of ritual.
Rising early, the bride bathes and waits to be presented; at dawn, the assistant presents the bride to her father-in-law and mother-in-law. She carries a basket with dates, chestnuts, and dried meat to present herself. The assistant offers sweet wine to the bride, and the bride offers sacrifices of dried meat and minced meat, and sacrifices the sweet wine, completing the bride's ritual. The father-in-law and mother-in-law enter the chamber, and the bride presents them with a suckling pig,
