zh:
东海往北，为勃海。前唐张守节《史记正义》云，“蓬莱、方丈、瀛洲，勃海中三神山也。”
不独仙山神岛，南接黄河，北纳滹沱，百川归流，亦是一大气象。
盖此为访仙之胜地，游赏之径要。
只是近日天公不美，风雨大作。怒海惊涛下，连捕鱼的渔人都舍了生计，停船罢橹。
偏那不知从哪里来的俩少年人，乘了一叶扁舟，往那勃海深处驶去。
着文人巾的立船头，迎风雨而歌。披鹤羽氅的站船尾，沐惊浪而棹。
“海色动远山，天鸡已先鸣。银台出倒景，白浪翻长鲸！”。船头少年的歌声，透过电闪雷鸣，穿到滚滚黑云间。
“好啊，到底是你个动嘴皮子的嗓子敞亮！”船尾的鹤衣少年，亦是朗笑。他看着远处溟濛的勃海深处，想着他们二人，游学归来，只是忽地一个兴之所至，便折到了这勃海之上，寻一物事。
兴之所起，在林险生。陪兴之人，是他萧鹤衣。
只是，他也好奇，林险生要来这一片空荡荡的大海，到底要寻的是何物？
是仙山？不，不会。林险生从不是雅好仙逸的人物。他们到过洛水，也踏足过终南。仙家逸事已矣，路过时，不过驻足一观，转眼便作云烟去。
是异宝？不，也不会。且休说他二人未曾将珠玉放在心上，更遑论这四处游历所携的行囊里，只一书卷，一长剑，一笔砚。若是为财，四处讨文墨者多，又何必冒此惊涛骇浪，赶赴险地。
可林险生就是卖关子，这是文津馆里，那些博古通今的学者通病。可越这样，萧鹤衣便越好奇。偏一放眼，这茫茫的海上，烟波浩渺，独独瞧不见甚物事。
林险生知道萧鹤衣心中所痒，却也不答。只唱“波荡落星湾”，“月晕天风雾不开”。他所求，确在海中。只是书中所记，史册所载，不曾亲眼窥见。既然此际乘兴之至，何不一睹痛快？
他求的，不是别物，是那海中的传说，鲸。
此番回文津馆的途中，偶然听得老农言说此物。便折返北上，寻那巨鲸的踪迹。林险生自幼熟读经文，早起《左传》，近至李杜韩孟，谈鲸者不少。但真要论懂鲸的，未必如海边渔户。
风浪大起的时候，是最容易见到鲸的时候。他想这一遭，想了很久了。
他想见，想见“刺手拨鲸牙，举瓢酌天浆”，想见“拾月鲸口边，何人免为吞”，想见“海鲸始生尾，试摆蓬壶涡”。哪怕那渔户，追着劝他，“少年人，那大鱼危险着咧！”
可少年的人，是最听不进劝的。一股热劲儿，从他的心底直往外涌，哪怕于这险浪中。
他想过很多与鲸相见的情形，想过与那大鱼擦身而过，想过那大鱼将他吞入鱼腹。想到萧鹤衣从他念叨的词儿里，终于明白他所想。
“险生，你是在寻鲸？”萧鹤衣摇橹的眸子，一下子亮了起来。
“你说，这鲸……该长什么样？”
林险生细想了想，道：“晋人崔豹《古今注》言，鲸大者长千里，小者数千丈。鼓浪成雷，喷沫成雨，水族畏，悉逃匿，鱼无敢当者。”
“南朝梁人任昉《述异记》又言，南海有珠，即鲸鱼目瞳，夜可以鉴，谓之夜光。”
林险生又顿了顿，“所谓闻雷霆而觉布鼓之陋，见巨鲸而知寸介之细。这书中记载鲸貌如何，到底还是要自己看过才是。”
萧鹤衣看着那茫茫一片的海，看着那船头吟哦领航的友人，心下也开始念着见鲸。
雷霆、巨浪、暴雨、狂风！来吧，再来猛烈些！
en:
North of the East Sea lies the Bohai Sea. Zhang Shoujie of the Tang Dynasty wrote in the Correct Meanings of the Shiji's Records: "Penglai, Fangzhang, and Yingzhou are the three divine mountains in the Bohai Sea." But this place is not known for myths alone. Bounded by the Yellow River to the south and the Hutuo River to the north, it is a grand spectacle where countless rivers converge. It has always been a famous destination for seeking immortals and a prime route for sightseeing.
Lately, however, the weather has turned vicious. Wind and rain tear across the sea. Under the raging waves, even the local fishermen have halted their work, dropping their anchors and putting away their oars. Yet, right at a time like this, two young men from nowhere took a small skiff and headed straight into the turbulent depths of the Bohai Sea.
The one at the bow, wearing a scholar's cap, sang into the wind and rain. The one at the stern, draped in a crane-feather cloak, rowed through the crashing swells.
"The sea's color stirs the distant hills; the celestial rooster has crowed before dawn. Silver terraces rise in mirrored light; white waves roll the great whales!" The boy at the bow sang so brightly that his voice pierced the thunder and lightning, reaching into the heavy black clouds above.
"Brilliant! Even the storm cannot drown out your voice!" The boy in the crane cloak laughed aloud from the stern. Looking toward the dim, misty reaches of the Bohai Sea, he thought of how they ended up here. They were returning from their academic travels when, on a sudden whim, they detoured to this sea in search of a specific thing.
The whim belonged to Lin Xiansheng. The one indulging it was Xiao Heyi.
Still, he could not help but wonder what exactly Lin Xiansheng had come all this way to find in this empty stretch of ocean.
An immortal mountain? No, surely not. Lin Xiansheng was not the sort to chase ethereal tales. They had visited the Luo River and set foot on Mount Zhongnan. Stories of immortals were just passing sights to him, fading like mist the moment he turned away.
Exotic treasures? No, not that either. Leaving aside that neither cared much for pearls or jade, they traveled light wherever they went: one scroll, one long sword, one brush, and one inkstone. If it were money he wanted, there were plenty of people seeking his calligraphy. Why brave these monstrous waves for wealth?
But Lin Xiansheng liked to keep people guessing. It was a common trait among the learned scholars of the Inkbound Order. And the less he said, the more curious Xiao Heyi became. Yet when he looked around, all he saw was the vast, misty sea, with absolutely nothing in sight.
Lin Xiansheng knew exactly what was on Xiao Heyi's mind, but he would not answer. He only kept singing lines like "Waves sweep Luoxing Bay," and "The moon is ringed, wind and mist seal the sky." What he wanted was indeed in the sea. He had read about it in books and historical records but had never seen it with his own eyes. Since the mood had struck, why not witness it to his heart's content?
What he sought was no ordinary object. It was the legend of the sea: the whale.
On his way back to the Inkbound Order, he had happened to hear an old farmer speak of this creature. Thus, he turned north to chase the giant whale. Lin Xiansheng had read widely since childhood. From the ancient Zuo Tradition to the poems of Li Bai, Du Fu, Han Yu, and Meng Jiao, many wrote about whales. But when it came to truly understanding them, scholars might not match the coastal fishermen.
When the wind and waves are at their highest, they said, whales are easiest to spot. He had wanted to make this trip for a very long time.
He wanted to see the scenes from the poems. He wanted to see "Reaching out to pluck the whale's teeth, raising a gourd to drink the heavenly nectar." He wanted to see "Scooping the moon by the whale's mouth, who could avoid being swallowed?" He wanted to see "The sea whale newly grown its tail, testing the whirlpools of Penglai." Even when the fishermen ran after him shouting, "Young man, that giant fish is dangerous!", he did not stop.
Youth rarely listens to warnings. A restless passion surged from his heart, fearless even in the face of these deadly waves.
He had imagined meeting the whale in many ways. He imagined brushing past the giant beast, or even being swallowed into its belly. Hearing the poetic lines Lin kept muttering, Xiao Heyi finally understood what he desired.
"Xiansheng, you're looking for a whale?" Xiao Heyi's eyes suddenly lit up as he pulled the oars.
"Tell me, what do you think a whale actually looks like?"
Lin Xiansheng thought it over, then said, "Cui Bao of the Jin Dynasty wrote in Notes on Antiquity and Today: The great whales are a thousand miles long, and the smaller ones measure thousands of fathoms. They beat the waves into thunder and blow spray into rain. All water creatures fear them and hide, and no fish dares stand in their path."
"Ren Fang of the Southern Dynasties wrote in Records of Strange Tales: There are pearls in the Southern Sea that are actually the pupils of whales. They shine at night and are called night-luminous pearls."
Lin Xiansheng paused, then continued, "As the saying goes: Only after hearing real thunder do you realize how weak a cloth drum sounds; only after seeing a giant whale do you know how tiny a shell is. No matter how the books describe its appearance, in the end, you have to see it for yourself."
Xiao Heyi looked out over the boundless sea, then back at his friend chanting at the bow. Deep down, he too began to crave the sight of the whale.
Thunder, giant waves, heavy rain, and howling winds! Come, let the storm be even fiercer!

zh:
唐末，江南盂城有优昙钵寺，以丹泉之井闻名，寺有一僧独居，号为善识。
天下战事频起，有白鹿负伤入寺，善识疗愈其伤，白鹿此后长居寺中，眷恋不去。
十余年后，众人于寺中礼佛，窥见僧房后有鹿冢，冢旁居一娉婷少女，自称鹿女。众人掌掴善识，责其污秽净地，又议将鹿女鬻卖于市，善识涕泪满面，百计莫阻。
鹿女替善识拭泪，合什下拜道：“吾将为长生母。”纵身投井。
彩云自井中起，托鹿女入重霄。众人拜呼仙人，欢喜赞叹而去。是夜，善识亦于井旁圆寂。
en:
In the late Tang Dynasty, in Yucheng of Jiangnan, stood Udumbara Temple, famed for its Pill Spring Well. A monk named Shanshi lived there alone. 
As wars ravaged the land, a wounded white deer sought refuge in the temple. Shanshi healed its wounds, and the deer lingered, unwilling to leave. 
Over a decade later, during a worship ceremony, villagers caught sight of a deer tomb behind Shanshi's quarters—and beside it, a graceful maiden calling herself the Deer Maiden. Enraged, they slapped Shanshi for desecrating the holy site and planned to sell the maiden. As Shanshi wept helplessly, no amount of pleading could stop them. 
The Deer Maiden wiped Shanshi's tears, clasped her hands, and said: "I shall be the mother of immortality." Then she leaped into the well. 
Colored clouds surged from the well, lifting her to the sky. The villagers hailed her as an immortal and departed in awe. That night, Shanshi passed away in meditation by the well.

zh:
致雩真。
我终于再次写下你的名字，离你不跟我说话，已经两年四十二天了。你还好吗？
今岁冬寒尤甚，犹记你说过，与师父初见时，亦是此时节。
那个孤零零的小女孩，瞪着那个笑吟吟的白须老翁，非但没把他瞪走，还瞪成了她的师父，她的爷爷。
爷爷是真心叫的，他把你最喜欢的剑给了你。
后来他走了，还带走了那把剑。但你这次不瞪他了，因为他说，那把剑迟早是你的，你会成为天下第一
可我认识你时，你手里却空无一物。
那时的你，只是一个哭泣的、无助的小女孩。你千里迢迢赶来，却被大大的奠字拦在门外。
你再也见不到爷爷了。可你的剑还在等你，在那个小小的木匣之中。
他们把你推出来，摔在地上，你又一遍遍地站起来，走上前去。
“那是我的剑”你哭着，“可是爷爷说，那是我的剑。”
我看着她，像一颗瘦瘦小小的钉子，倔强地扎进了雪地里。
后来，你还是走了。因你遇着了她。
她说，拿得住的东西才是你的。一味哭求，最是无用。
那时我就站在你身边，心里忽然有些怕，不知该把你的手再牵紧一点，还是松开一点。
你乘上她的车子，去了邙山。
再后来，便是那天夜里。我在宫外等你，等到山陵崩的钟声，你终于出来，沉默地向前走去，一直走一直走，我便一直跟在你后头
直走到悬崖边。
月亮落下来了，你说：阿尧，为什么我总是来得太晚。
你还没来得及，为这个权倾天下又孤独病逝的女人做任何事。
我师父常说，心病难治。因其久，因其深。你不信，你找到了一个可以治的人，太平公主，她的女儿。
公主说：你和无量先师，便如我和天后一般。你只略略看到她母亲的影子，就一头撞了进去。
雩真，你素来聪慧胜我，剑术胜我，心性胜我，却何以甘从执剑之人，沦为他人手中之剑呢？
冬夜雪地，天地虚白，你从公主府摇摇晃晃而来，一身血染。我把很多很多药敷在你身上，也把很多很多话砸向你，痛苦的话，愤怒的话，伤人的话，无济于事的话。
而你只是垂着头，不发一言。
我知道，我治不好你的病了。于是雪停的时候，我走了。
冬日暖阳如火，善照天下有情人、有怨事。只是它照不到我了，雩真。
两年四十二天，我晒了很多药，也治好了很多人。直到你和狐令飞约战的消息传来。
我忽然发现，我还是很想你，很担心你。
想着也许……你会需要我呢。
等回过神来，信已经写到了这里。人也已经在路上了。
我能去见你吗？如果见到你，你会和我说话吗？如果见到你，我能和你说话吗？
如果我们说话，又会说什么呢？
也许什么都不说。就只是像第一次交换名字时那样，两个人静静地看着冰面，看了许久，小小的你忽然抽出剑来，一剑划过
凌冽的冰上，腾起一尾尾鲜活的鱼，你回头看我，鼻尖红红的，轻声问，请你吃鱼，要么？
我始终很乐意的。
en:
My dearest Yuzhen.
I'm finally writing your name again. It's been two years and forty-two days since you last spoke to me. Are you well?
This winter's colder than most. I remember you telling me you first met your master at this time of year.
That lonely little girl, glaring at the smiling, white-bearded old man. But her glare didn't drive him away. Instead, he became her master, her grandfather.
You called him grandfather in earnest, and he gave you the sword you loved most.
Later, he left, taking the sword with him. But you didn't glare at him this time, because he said that sword would be yours one day, that you would become the Greatest Under Heaven.
But when I met you, your hands were empty.
You were just a weeping, helpless little girl. You had traveled so far, only to be stopped by the mourning banners at the gate.
You would never see your grandfather again. But your sword was waiting for you, inside that small wooden box.
They shoved you out, threw you to the ground, but you stood back up and walked forward, again and again.
"That's my sword," you cried. "Grandfather said that's my sword!"
I watched a thin, tiny nail being driven stubbornly into the snow.
In the end, you left. Because you met her.
She told you that only what you can hold onto is truly yours. Crying and begging gets you nothing.
I was standing right beside you, and was suddenly afraid. I didn't know whether to hold your hand tighter, or to let it go.
You departed for Mount Mang, after climbing into her carriage.
And then came that night. I waited for you outside the palace until the funeral bells tolled. You finally emerged, walking forward in silence. You kept walking, and I followed close behind.
We walked all the way to the edge of a cliff. The moon had set, and you said, "Yao, why am I always too late?"
You never had the chance to do anything for her. The woman who once held the world in her hands, yet died alone in sickness.
My master always said that ailments of the heart are the hardest to cure, for they run long and deep. You didn't believe it. You found someone you thought could cure you: Princess Taiping. Her daughter.
The Princess said, "You and Master Wuliang are just like me and the Empress." You caught the faintest glimpse of her mother in her, and threw yourself right in.
Yuzhen, you've always been smarter than me, a better swordswoman, stronger of heart. So why were you content to go from wielder of swords to a sword wielded by another?
That snowy winter night, when the world was a void of white, you staggered out of the Princess's manor, drenched in blood. I put so much medicine on your wounds, threw so many words at you. Words of pain, words of anger. Words meant to hurt. Words of no avail.
But you just hung your head in silence.
I knew then I couldn't cure you. So when the snow stopped, I left.
The winter sun burns like fire, shining on all the lovers and grievances in the world. But, Yuzhen, it no longer shines on me.
Two years and forty-two days have passed. I've dried many herbs and healed many people. Then, word of your duel with Hu Lingfei reached me.
And suddenly I realized, I still miss you. I still worry about you. I thought, maybe... you might need me.
Before I knew it, I had already written this much. And I was already on my way.
Can I come see you? If I do, will you speak to me? If I do, can I speak to you?
And if we do speak, what would we even say?
Perhaps nothing at all. Just like the first time we exchanged names. Just the two of us, gazing quietly at the frozen lake, for a long time. Then, you will suddenly draw your sword, and with a single slash...
...pull a lively fish from the icy water. You'll turn to look at me, your nose red from the cold, and ask softly, "Would you like some fish?"
I would, Yuzhen. And I always will.

老僧残记·其一

建隆四年，荆湖兵乱，流民沿江而来，欲入钱塘。
然队伍中已有疫者。
发热，咳血，起疹。
城门不开，乡里不纳。
他们退无可退，宿于庙中。
我不忍逐之。

闻城中回春堂凡有病苦，不问贵贱，皆愿施治。已遣大弟子入城，持信往请。若有医者愿意来庙，救此一众苦命之人……
en:
Fragments from an Old Monk's Journal: Part I

In the fourth year of Jianlong, war ravaged Jingzhou. A tide of refugees fled down the river, seeking refuge in Qiantang.
But a plague had already crept into their ranks, bringing fevers, the coughing of blood, and angry rashes.
The city bolted its gates, and the local villages turned them away.
With nowhere left to turn, they sought refuge in the temple.
I could not find it in my heart to drive them out.

Word has it that the Spring's Return Hall in the city heals all who suffer, asking nothing of their wealth or station. I have dispatched my senior disciple into the city, bearing a letter of entreaty. If only a doctor might brave the journey to our temple, to treat these suffering souls...

北小鱼深知，洪四最初建无忧洞，并无对抗九流门之意。洪四只是想让像自己一样不被世人所容之人，有处可栖。虽然血仇面前他们无从辩解，但他心怀希望，时间会治愈一切。

但郭威攻城那日，因九流门人，洪四失去了他的父母。自此一切都变了。他改名洪肆，扩无忧洞，立无忧帮，广纳天下恶徒，誓要将九流门一网打尽。

再后来，洪肆带着一对兄妹离开了开封。而留下来的北小鱼，只能眼见着无忧洞成为恶人群聚之地。 在被恶匪弃于水下之时，北小鱼终于心生绝望。
他深知，此后这无忧洞，将再无生路。
en:
Bei Xiaoyu knew that Hong never built the Unbound Cavern to oppose the Nine Mortal Ways. He only wanted a place for those like himself, unwanted, outcast, a place to belong. Though their hands were stained with blood, he still believed time would mend the wounds. 

But the day Guo Wei's army stormed the city, the Nine Mortal Ways' schemes cost Hong his parents. And everything changed. He changed his name to Hong Si, expanded the Unbound Cavern, and welcomed scoundrels from across the world. He vowed to wipe the Nine Mortal Ways from the earth. 

Later, Hong Si left Kaifeng with a pair of siblings. And the one who stayed behind, Bei Xiaoyu, could only watch as Unbound Cavern turned into a haven for monsters. When the thugs cast him into the waters to drown, desperation finally took root in his heart. 
He knew all too well, there would be no hope in Unbound Cavern from this moment on.

zh: 上版，雕版之工序也。写样既成，以面粉熬糊，将写样反贴于梨枣木版之上。待纸背麇茸，轻刷去浮屑，反字即毕现于版面，遂可付梓。此法最考验匠心，糊厚则渗墨而污版，糊薄则易脱落。纸上纸下，须纹理贴切，方见精细。
en:
Manuscript transfer is a crucial step in woodblock printing. Once the master copy is written, it is pasted face-down onto a polished pearwood or jujube woodblock using a paste made from boiled flour. When dry, the artisan gently rubs away the back layers of the paper and brushes off loose fibers, leaving the reversed characters clearly visible on the wood for carving.
This process requires precise judgment: paste applied too thickly will bleed ink and ruin the block, while paste applied too thinly will cause the paper to peel.

zh: 白马之祸后，文津馆中藏书由弟子们带走，藏书自此散佚各地。长乐老半生奔波，将北方藏书大半寻回，而失散于南方的部分经典却成了世家私藏。后世宗南征，林险生借机南下，欲将合并南北典藏，有人为阻南书北归，派人追击。学子文人不惜以身躯为盾、为墙，更有人将纸页顶在头上投身江中，宁愿葬身江水也要将书送归。自此之后，文津馆典籍馆藏南北合龙，此事在实录中被记为“纸片渡江”。
en: In the wake of the Baima Incident, the Inkbound Order's collected texts were carried away by its disciples and scattered to the far corners of the land. Elder Changle spent half his life wandering in search of them, recovering the greater part of those lost in the north, yet the volumes that had drifted south fell into the private hoards of powerful clans. When Emperor Shizong later led his campaign southward, Lin Xiansheng seized the opportunity to follow, intent on uniting the northern and southern collections at last. Those who wished to prevent the southern texts from returning north sent men in pursuit. Scholars and men of letters threw themselves forward as human shields, and some, placing loose pages atop their heads, cast themselves into the river, choosing to be swallowed by its waters rather than let the books fail to reach their home. From that day forth, the Inkbound Order's collections from north and south were joined as one, and the deed was set down in the chronicles as "Boat of Paper."

古乐是个谦谦君子，擅抚琴却不擅言语，仇越海知道，也总喜欢逗他。
我与你烈言兄弟同时落入水中，你救谁？
噔地一声，被这无理的问题惊到，古乐的琴都弹错了一声。
都救，都救。
不成，你这副身板，能救上一个已经了不起，怎么都救？
那便……唉……
古乐说不清楚，只好苦笑。
你们一个两个，就不能自己游水上来么？

古乐和仇越海第一次见面的时候，见到一个渔夫打扮的少年人，叼着小麦草翘脚躺在屋顶上假寐。
那天天气很好，太阳很盛，少年嘴里的小麦草金黄金黄。
那时古乐刚刚接受烈言的邀约，前来一同抗击契丹，于是忍着强光，眯眼抬头询问。
请问……烈言兄弟是在这么？
烈言兄弟？……叫这么亲，你是他兄还是他弟？
少年睁眼看他，坏心眼地揶揄。
不是……我们并非亲生兄弟，只是……
不是亲生兄弟，莫非是继兄继弟？
也不是……我们并无这种关系……只是我在弹琴，烈言兄弟他、他……
古乐一时情急，也不知道怎么说这来龙去脉了。认栽垂头。
总之，他叫我来。
那少年哈哈大笑，从屋顶上跳下来。
我知道我知道，你也是跟着那家伙来打契丹人的吧。
我也是，我叫仇越海，若你愿意，也可以称我一声兄弟。
仇越海拍了拍他的肩，似乎是表示歉意。
不好意思啊，不知怎的，见了你这傻乎乎的公子哥，总想欺负你几句。

后来有了河东八俊的名号，古乐和仇越海真成了拜把子的兄弟。
高山流水的公子哥和出身草野的渔夫，竟也有几分钟子期与伯牙的味道。
于是常能见到这么一幕：
古乐冥思苦想，绞尽脑汁，对着来人不知如何解释，只好出口一个“总之……”。
而一旁的仇越海，却听懂了古乐的意思，“是这样……”，一五一十地解释给对面听。
其他人都笑称他们二人，为“总之”、“是这样”兄弟，所谓知音，便也就是如此了吧？
他们少年时的情谊之深、相见之欢，由此可见一斑。而后来的分道扬镳，皆为后话，与此有别。
en:
Gu Le was the kind of refined soul whose emotions flowed effortlessly through his guqin, yet whose tongue seemed to stumble over every word. Qiu Yuehai knew this well and loved teasing him.
"If your brother Lie Yan and I both fell into the river, who would you save?"
Pluck! The absurd question made Gu Le miss a note.
"Both! I'd save both!"
"Impossible. With your frame, saving one would be a miracle enough."
"Then... ah..." Flustered, Gu Le could only sigh.
"Must you two drown yourselves at all?"

When they first met, Gu Le saw a fisherman-looking youth lounging on a rooftop, golden wheat stalk between his teeth. Bright sunlight that day. The stalk inside his mouth gleamed like gold. Newly recruited by Lie Yan to resist the Khitans, Gu Le squinted upward:
"Excuse me... is Brother Lie Yan here?"
"Brother Lie Yan? You two sound close? Are you his real brother?"
The youth's teasing eyes sparkled with mischief.
"No... we're not related, it's just..."
"Stepbrothers then?"
"No... No relation at all! I was playing guqin when Lie Yan..." Red-faced, Gu Le gave up explaining and let his head drop.
"Anyway, he asked me to come."
The youth laughed, jumping down.
"I know, I know. Another recruit against the Khitan! I am here for that too. I'm Qiu Yuehai. Call me brother if you like."
Qiu Yuehai patted his shoulder, perhaps an apology.
"Sorry, but whenever I meet earnest young gentlemen like you, I can't help wanting to tease you."

Later, when they became famed as two of the "Eight Talents of Hedong," their bond deepened. The refined aristocrat and the rough fisherman were modern Zhong Ziqi and Bo Ya. Their dynamic became legendary:
Gu Le struggles to explain, always starting with "Anyway..."
Qiu Yuehai instantly understood: "What he means is..."
Others called them the "Anyway" and "What he means" brothers. Such was their harmony. Their youthful camaraderie burned bright. What came after belongs to another story.

The all-new Hexi region, the fresh season "Harmony of Jiazhong," and stunning new cosmetics are now available following the March 28, 2025 update! To help all adventurers reap bountiful rewards and prepare for the new chapter, here’s a breakdown of Version 1.7 "Moonlight Over Jade Gate":  

### I. New Region Unveiled  
The winds beyond Hexi’s frontier carry not only sweeping vistas but also tales of romance and heroism woven into poetry. Inspired by legends, the heroic deeds of warriors transcend time, their voices echoing once more.  
- <LINK id='link1' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60311' is_underline='true'>[Unlock]</LINK> Hexi Region  
- <LINK id='link2' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60312' is_underline='true'>[Explore]</LINK> Jade Gate Moon Chronicles  
- <LINK id='link3' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60313' is_underline='true'>[Challenge]</LINK> Hexi Martial Records  

### II. New Gameplay & Events  
1. The new Martial Style "Bamboo Breaker: Dust" debuts, alongside the umbrella-based "Spring Dreamscape" and rope dart technique "Fleeting Clouds." <LINK id='link4' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60314' is_underline='true'>[Learn More]</LINK>  
2. Participate in "Resonance" for a chance to win the new outfit set "Moonlit Claws" and hairstyle accessory "Dancing Moonlight." <LINK id='link5' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60315' is_underline='true'>[Learn More]</LINK>  

### III. New Cosmetics  
1. Limited-time outfit "Desert Cavalry" now in shop. <LINK id='link6' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60316' is_underline='true'>[View]</LINK>  
2. New spear skin "Bamboo Spear" available. <LINK id='link7' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60317' is_underline='true'>[View]</LINK>  
3. "Spring Dreamscape" visual effect "Ink-Stained Dust" added. <LINK id='link8' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60318' is_underline='true'>[View]</LINK>  
4. "Fleeting Clouds" effect "Wind Plays Eternity" now in shop. <LINK id='link9' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60319' is_underline='true'>[View]</LINK>  
5. New headgear "Little Mouser" released. <LINK id='link10' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60320' is_underline='true'>[View]</LINK>  

### IV. New Season Updates  
1. Added solo mode tier "Twelfth Rank: Wuwei," allowing max level 81. Tier 81 Gear is now obtainable, with Tier 71 Gear Vault unlocked. Upgrades for "Harmonics," "Mystic Skill Breakthrough," and "Medicine Box" expanded. <LINK id='link11' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60321' is_underline='true'>[Details]</LINK>  
2. Enhanced progression for Gear, Martial Styles, Mystic Skills, and Inner Way, including smoother Tier 81 Gear acquisition. New features: "Tuning" (adjust gear stats), "Transpose" (convert Martial Style insights), and guaranteed Mystic Skill material drops. <LINK id='link12' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60322' is_underline='true'>[Details]</LINK>  
3. Class balance adjustments based on "Golden Bell Season" feedback. <LINK id='link13' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60314' is_underline='true'>[Details]</LINK>  
4. Battle Pass "Harmony of Jiazhong I" now live. <LINK id='link14' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60323' is_underline='true'>[Details]</LINK>  
5. "Taiping Tomb: Style Trials" Season 1 begins. <LINK id='link15' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60324' is_underline='true'>[Details]</LINK>  
6. Added 10-player Hero's Realm "Sorrows of Mortal Dust (Extreme)" and 5-player duel "Drunken Shadows." <LINK id='link16' color='#8c5823' goto_id='839' is_underline='true'>[Details]</LINK>  
7. "Industries War Preseason" starts—compete Mon/Wed/Fri 8–11 PM. <LINK id='link17' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60326' is_underline='true'>[Details]</LINK>  
8. "Blade’s End" PvP season reset with tier adjustments for "Duel," "Clash," "Arena," "World Contention," and "Forest of Awakening." <LINK id='link18' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60327' is_underline='true'>[Details]</LINK>  
9. Added "Basic Talents" and "Boss Talents," with "Blade’s End Talents" reset. <LINK id='link19' color='#8c5823' goto_id='60328' is_underline='true'>[Details]</LINK>

en:
Many noble houses of Hangzhou brewed their own wine. Chen Zixi was fond of drinking, and his elder brother Chen Zizhen, borrowing the name of the Spring's Return Hall, arranged for a batch of medicinal wine to be brewed.
Steeped with over a dozen warming, nourishing herbs, prolonged drinking was said to strengthen the sinews and bones, fortify the root and nurture the origin. The taste, too, was superb, smooth and mellow upon entry, the complex herbal notes carefully wrapped within the wine's aroma. At first taste, it was strange yet fresh, leaving a lingering sweetness in the throat after swallowing.
On the first opening of the jar, Chen Zixi drank it to the very bottom in one go, only then remembering that the wine was meant to nourish the body.

张球曾用这支笔写下了万千诗行，也曾为挚友写下请节的奏折。
他曾豪言，要为友人作传，供世人敬仰。

可最后，他连为他写一首诗都做不到。
褚修气绝，号恸呕血，他今日之心，亦如毁卒。
悲愤不可忍，冷气不能食。
en:
A brush, ink long dried, its shaft polished smooth. 

Zhang Qiu once wrote countless poems with it, and petitions pleading for his friend's honor. 
He vowed to write his friend's biography for all to admire. 

But in the end, he couldn't even compose a single poem for him. 
Chu Xiu is gone—wailing, vomiting blood. Today, my heart feels like a fallen soldier. 
Grief unbearable, cold air chokes all appetite.

周边，是热闹的人海，有力的叫卖；身边，是爹爹的守护，亲人的叮咛。

这是郑然的肯定。
en:
Father said this year would be a good one.
Father also said that Sushan Ice Cream is sweet, just like Lotus Pastry is sweet.
Zheng Ran held her father's big hand tight and followed him, walking slowly forward.
Around them was a bustling sea of people and energetic cries of vendors; beside her, her father's protection and family's gentle words.
The Sushan Ice Cream was also delicious.
This was Zheng Ran's conclusion.

Qiu Yuehai, a man from the lands of Jin, was famed for his mastery of the twelve-foot spear. With lightness skill and peerless technique, he could leap as though treading among the stars; his spear tip seemed fit to challenge even the mighty Kunpeng. Those who saw his heroic bearing called him a true champion among men. It was said at the time: "We may not see Liezi riding the wind, but in Lord Qiu's soaring dance, he seems to grasp the sun and moon themselves!"
I once heard that, beneath an ancient tree in Qinghe, a dozen wine jars were arranged like stars in the sky. A hero passed among them with a spear in hand—moving so swiftly, not a single drop of wine was spilled, nor did a flower petal stir in the breeze. People called him the #YWine Jar Celestial#E. Looking back now, I believe that must have been none other than Qiu Yuehai himself.
